units.leftText: This is the beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.
units.rightText: The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.
leftNotes: 1:1 ECM, NE, BYZ, and TR; SBL and WH the beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ.

units.leftText: As it is written in Isaiah the prophet: “Behold, I will send My messenger ahead of You, who will prepare Your way.”
units.rightText: Even as it is written in Isaiah the prophet, Behold, I send my messenger before thy face, Who shall prepare thy way;
leftNotes: 1:2 BYZ and TR in the prophets:
1:2 Malachi 3:1|MAL 3:1*

units.leftText: “A voice of one calling in the wilderness, ‘Prepare the way for the Lord, make straight paths for Him.’”
units.rightText: The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Make ye ready the way of the Lord, Make his paths straight;
leftNotes: 1:3 Isaiah 40:3|ISA 40:3* (see also LXX)

units.leftText: John the Baptist appeared in the wilderness, preaching a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins.
units.rightText: John came, who baptized in the wilderness and preached the baptism of repentance unto remission of sins.

units.leftText: People went out to him from all of Jerusalem and the countryside of Judea. Confessing their sins, they were baptized by him in the Jordan River.
units.rightText: And there went out unto him all the country of Judæa, and all they of Jerusalem; and they were baptized of him in the river Jordan, confessing their sins.

units.leftText: John was clothed in camel’s hair, with a leather belt around his waist. His food was locusts and wild honey.
units.rightText: And John was clothed with camel’s hair, and had a leathern girdle about his loins, and did eat locusts and wild honey.

units.leftText: And he proclaimed: “After me will come One more powerful than I, the straps of whose sandals I am not worthy to stoop down and untie.
units.rightText: And he preached, saying, There cometh after me he that is mightier than I, the latchet of whose shoes I am not worthy to stoop down and unloose.

units.leftText: I baptize you with water, but He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit. ”
units.rightText: I baptized you in water; but he shall baptize you in the Holy Spirit.
leftNotes: 1:8 Or in water
1:8 Or in the Holy Spirit

units.leftText: In those days Jesus came from Nazareth in Galilee and was baptized by John in the Jordan.
units.rightText: And it came to pass in those days, that Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee, and was baptized of John in the Jordan.

units.leftText: As soon as Jesus came up out of the water, He saw the heavens breaking open and the Spirit descending on Him like a dove.
units.rightText: And straightway coming up out of the water, he saw the heavens rent asunder, and the Spirit as a dove descending upon him:
leftNotes: 1:10 Or he saw; see John 1:32–33|JHN 1:32-33*

units.leftText: And a voice came from heaven: “You are My beloved Son; in You I am well pleased.” The Temptation and Preaching of Jesus (Matthew 4:1–17|MAT 4:1-17*; Luke 4:1–15|LUK 4:1-15*)
units.rightText: and a voice came out of the heavens, Thou art my beloved Son, in thee I am well pleased.

units.leftText: At once the Spirit drove Jesus into the wilderness,
units.rightText: And straightway the Spirit driveth him forth into the wilderness.

units.leftText: and He was there for forty days, being tempted by Satan. He was with the wild animals, and the angels ministered to Him.
units.rightText: And he was in the wilderness forty days tempted of Satan; and he was with the wild beasts; and the angels ministered unto him.

units.leftText: After the arrest of John, Jesus went into Galilee and proclaimed the gospel of God.
units.rightText: Now after John was delivered up, Jesus came into Galilee, preaching the gospel of God,
leftNotes: 1:14 BYZ and TR the gospel of the kingdom of God

units.leftText: “The time is fulfilled,” He said, “and the kingdom of God is near. Repent and believe in the gospel!” The First Disciples (Matthew 4:18–22|MAT 4:18-22*; Luke 5:1–11|LUK 5:1-11*; John 1:35–42|JHN 1:35-42*)
units.rightText: and saying, The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand: repent ye, and believe in the gospel.

units.leftText: As Jesus was walking beside the Sea of Galilee, He saw Simon and his brother Andrew. They were casting a net into the sea, for they were fishermen.
units.rightText: And passing along by the sea of Galilee, he saw Simon and Andrew the brother of Simon casting a net in the sea; for they were fishers.

units.leftText: “Come, follow Me,” Jesus said, “and I will make you fishers of men.”
units.rightText: And Jesus said unto them, Come ye after me, and I will make you to become fishers of men.

units.leftText: And at once they left their nets and followed Him.
units.rightText: And straightway they left the nets, and followed him.

units.leftText: Going on a little farther, He saw James son of Zebedee and his brother John. They were in a boat, mending their nets.
units.rightText: And going on a little further, he saw James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, who also were in the boat mending the nets.

units.leftText: Immediately Jesus called them, and they left their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired men and followed Him. Jesus Expels an Unclean Spirit (Luke 4:31–37|LUK 4:31-37*)
units.rightText: And straightway he called them: and they left their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired servants, and went after him.

units.leftText: Then Jesus and His companions went to Capernaum, and right away Jesus entered the synagogue on the Sabbath and began to teach.
units.rightText: And they go into Capernaum; and straightway on the sabbath day he entered into the synagogue and taught.

units.leftText: The people were astonished at His teaching, because He taught as one who had authority, and not as the scribes.
units.rightText: And they were astonished at his teaching: for he taught them as having authority, and not as the scribes.

units.leftText: Suddenly a man with an unclean spirit cried out in the synagogue:
units.rightText: And straightway there was in their synagogue a man with an unclean spirit; and he cried out,

units.leftText: “What do You want with us, Jesus of Nazareth? Have You come to destroy us? I know who You are — the Holy One of God!”
units.rightText: saying, What have we to do with thee, Jesus thou Nazarene? art thou come to destroy us? I know thee who thou art, the Holy One of God.

units.leftText: But Jesus rebuked the spirit. “Be silent!” He said. “Come out of him!”
units.rightText: And Jesus rebuked him, saying, Hold thy peace, and come out of him.

units.leftText: At this, the unclean spirit threw the man into convulsions and came out with a loud shriek.
units.rightText: And the unclean spirit, tearing him and crying with a loud voice, came out of him.

units.leftText: All the people were amazed and began to ask one another, “What is this? A new teaching with authority! He commands even the unclean spirits, and they obey Him!”
units.rightText: And they were all amazed, insomuch that they questioned among themselves, saying, What is this? a new teaching! with authority he commandeth even the unclean spirits, and they obey him.

units.leftText: And the news about Jesus spread quickly through the whole region of Galilee. Jesus Heals at Peter’s House (Matthew 8:14–17|MAT 8:14-17*; Luke 4:38–41|LUK 4:38-41*)
units.rightText: And the report of him went out straightway everywhere into all the region of Galilee round about.

units.leftText: As soon as Jesus and His companions had left the synagogue, they went with James and John to the home of Simon and Andrew.
units.rightText: And straightway, when they were come out of the synagogue, they came into the house of Simon and Andrew, with James and John.

units.leftText: Simon’s mother-in-law was sick in bed with a fever, and they promptly told Jesus about her.
units.rightText: Now Simon’s wife’s mother lay sick of a fever; and straightway they tell him of her:

units.leftText: So He went to her, took her by the hand, and helped her up. The fever left her, and she began to serve them.
units.rightText: and he came and took her by the hand, and raised her up; and the fever left her, and she ministered unto them.

units.leftText: That evening, after sunset, people brought to Jesus all the sick and demon-possessed,
units.rightText: And at even, when the sun did set, they brought unto him all that were sick, and them that were possessed with demons.

units.leftText: and the whole town gathered at the door.
units.rightText: And all the city was gathered together at the door.

units.leftText: And He healed many who were ill with various diseases and drove out many demons. But He would not allow the demons to speak, because they knew who He was. Jesus Prays and Preaches (Luke 4:42–44|LUK 4:42-44*)
units.rightText: And he healed many that were sick with divers diseases, and cast out many demons; and he suffered not the demons to speak, because they knew him.

units.leftText: Early in the morning, while it was still dark, Jesus got up and went out to a solitary place to pray.
units.rightText: And in the morning, a great while before day, he rose up and went out, and departed into a desert place, and there prayed.

units.leftText: Simon and his companions went to look for Him,
units.rightText: And Simon and they that were with him followed after him;

units.leftText: and when they found Him, they said, “Everyone is looking for You!”
units.rightText: and they found him, and say unto him, All are seeking thee.

units.leftText: But Jesus answered, “Let us go on to the neighboring towns so I can preach there as well, for that is why I have come.”
units.rightText: And he saith unto them, Let us go elsewhere into the next towns, that I may preach there also; for to this end came I forth.

units.leftText: So He went throughout Galilee, preaching in their synagogues and driving out demons. The Leper’s Prayer (Leviticus 14:1–32|LEV 14:1-32*; Matthew 8:1–4|MAT 8:1-4*; Luke 5:12–16|LUK 5:12-16*)
units.rightText: And he went into their synagogues throughout all Galilee, preaching and casting out demons.

units.leftText: Then a leper came to Jesus, begging on his knees: “If You are willing, You can make me clean.”
units.rightText: And there cometh to him a leper, beseeching him, and kneeling down to him, and saying unto him, If thou wilt, thou canst make me clean.
leftNotes: 1:40 A leper was one afflicted with a skin disease. See Leviticus 13.

units.leftText: Moved with compassion, Jesus reached out His hand and touched the man. “I am willing,” He said. “Be clean!”
units.rightText: And being moved with compassion, he stretched forth his hand, and touched him, and saith unto him, I will; be thou made clean.
leftNotes: 1:41 SBL Moved with indignation

units.leftText: And immediately the leprosy left him, and the man was cleansed.
units.rightText: And straightway the leprosy departed from him, and he was made clean.

units.leftText: Jesus promptly sent him away with a stern warning:
units.rightText: And he strictly charged him, and straightway sent him out,

units.leftText: “See that you don’t tell anyone. But go, show yourself to the priest and present the offering Moses prescribed for your cleansing, as a testimony to them.”
units.rightText: and saith unto him, See thou say nothing to any man: but go show thyself to the priest, and offer for thy cleansing the things which Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them.
leftNotes: 1:44 See Leviticus 14:1–32|LEV 14:1-32*.

units.leftText: But the man went out and openly began to proclaim and spread the news. Consequently, Jesus could no longer enter a town in plain view, but He stayed out in solitary places. Yet people came to Him from every quarter.
units.rightText: But he went out, and began to publish it much, and to spread abroad the matter, insomuch that Jesus could no more openly enter into a city, but was without in desert places: and they came to him from every quarter.

units.leftText: A few days later Jesus went back to Capernaum. And when the people heard that He was home,
units.rightText: And when he entered again into Capernaum after some days, it was noised that he was in the house.

units.leftText: they gathered in such large numbers that there was no more room, not even outside the door, as Jesus spoke the word to them.
units.rightText: And many were gathered together, so that there was no longer room for them, no, not even about the door: and he spake the word unto them.

units.leftText: Then a paralytic was brought to Him, carried by four men.
units.rightText: And they come, bringing unto him a man sick of the palsy, borne of four.

units.leftText: Since they were unable to get to Jesus through the crowd, they uncovered the roof above Him, made an opening, and lowered the paralytic on his mat.
units.rightText: And when they could not come nigh unto him for the crowd, they uncovered the roof where he was: and when they had broken it up, they let down the bed whereon the sick of the palsy lay.

units.leftText: When Jesus saw their faith, He said to the paralytic, “Son, your sins are forgiven.”
units.rightText: And Jesus seeing their faith saith unto the sick of the palsy, Son, thy sins are forgiven.

units.leftText: But some of the scribes were sitting there and thinking in their hearts,
units.rightText: But there were certain of the scribes sitting there, and reasoning in their hearts,

units.leftText: “Why does this man speak like this? He is blaspheming! Who can forgive sins but God alone?”
units.rightText: Why doth this man thus speak? he blasphemeth: who can forgive sins but one, even God?

units.leftText: At once Jesus knew in His spirit that they were thinking this way within themselves. “Why are you thinking these things in your hearts?” He asked.
units.rightText: And straightway Jesus, perceiving in his spirit that they so reasoned within themselves, saith unto them, Why reason ye these things in your hearts?

units.leftText: “Which is easier: to say to a paralytic, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up, pick up your mat, and walk’?
units.rightText: Which is easier, to say to the sick of the palsy, Thy sins are forgiven; or to say, Arise, and take up thy bed, and walk?

units.leftText: But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins...” He said to the paralytic,
units.rightText: But that ye may know that the Son of man hath authority on earth to forgive sins (he saith to the sick of the palsy),

units.leftText: “I tell you, get up, pick up your mat, and go home.”
units.rightText: I say unto thee, Arise, take up thy bed, and go unto thy house.

units.leftText: And immediately the man got up, picked up his mat, and walked out in front of them all. As a result, they were all astounded and glorified God, saying, “We have never seen anything like this!” Jesus Calls Levi (Matthew 9:9–13|MAT 9:9-13*; Luke 5:27–32|LUK 5:27-32*)
units.rightText: And he arose, and straightway took up the bed, and went forth before them all; insomuch that they were all amazed, and glorified God, saying, We never saw it on this fashion.

units.leftText: Once again Jesus went out beside the sea. All the people came to Him, and He taught them there.
units.rightText: And he went forth again by the sea side; and all the multitude resorted unto him, and he taught them.

units.leftText: As He was walking along, He saw Levi son of Alphaeus sitting at the tax booth. “Follow Me,” He told him, and Levi got up and followed Him.
units.rightText: And as he passed by, he saw Levi the son of Alphæus sitting at the place of toll, and he saith unto him, Follow me. And he arose and followed him.

units.leftText: While Jesus was dining at Levi’s house, many tax collectors and sinners were eating with Him and His disciples — for there were many who followed Him.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, that he was sitting at meat in his house, and many publicans and sinners sat down with Jesus and his disciples: for there were many, and they followed him.

units.leftText: When the scribes who were Pharisees saw Jesus eating with these people, they asked His disciples, “Why does He eat with tax collectors and sinners?”
units.rightText: And the scribes of the Pharisees, when they saw that he was eating with the sinners and publicans, said unto his disciples, How is it that he eateth and drinketh with publicans and sinners?
leftNotes: 2:16 BYZ and TR include and drink; see Luke 5:30|LUK 5:30*.

units.leftText: On hearing this, Jesus told them, “It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick. I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners.” Questions about Fasting (Matthew 9:14–15|MAT 9:14-15*; Luke 5:33–35|LUK 5:33-35*)
units.rightText: And when Jesus heard it, he saith unto them, They that are whole have no need of a physician, but they that are sick: I came not to call the righteous, but sinners.

units.leftText: Now John’s disciples and the Pharisees were often fasting. So people came to Jesus and asked, “Why don’t Your disciples fast like John’s disciples and those of the Pharisees?”
units.rightText: And John’s disciples and the Pharisees were fasting: and they come and say unto him, Why do John’s disciples and the disciples of the Pharisees fast, but thy disciples fast not?

units.leftText: Jesus replied, “How can the guests of the bridegroom fast while He is with them? As long as He is with them, they cannot fast.
units.rightText: And Jesus said unto them, Can the sons of the bridechamber fast, while the bridegroom is with them? as long as they have the bridegroom with them, they cannot fast.

units.leftText: But the time will come when the bridegroom will be taken from them; then they will fast. The Patches and the Wineskins (Matthew 9:16–17|MAT 9:16-17*; Luke 5:36–39|LUK 5:36-39*)
units.rightText: But the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken away from them, and then will they fast in that day.

units.leftText: No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment. If he does, the new piece will pull away from the old, and a worse tear will result.
units.rightText: No man seweth a piece of undressed cloth on an old garment: else that which should fill it up taketh from it, the new from the old, and a worse rent is made.

units.leftText: And no one pours new wine into old wineskins. If he does, the wine will burst the skins, and both the wine and the wineskins will be ruined. Instead, new wine is poured into new wineskins.” The Lord of the Sabbath (1 Samuel 21:1–7|1SA 21:1-7*; Matthew 12:1–8|MAT 12:1-8*; Luke 6:1–5|LUK 6:1-5*)
units.rightText: And no man putteth new wine into old wine-skins; else the wine will burst the skins, and the wine perisheth, and the skins: but they put new wine into fresh wine-skins.
leftNotes: 2:22 Tischendorf does not include Instead, new wine is poured into new wineskins.

units.leftText: One Sabbath Jesus was passing through the grainfields, and His disciples began to pick the heads of grain as they walked along.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, that he was going on the sabbath day through the grainfields; and his disciples began, as they went, to pluck the ears.

units.leftText: So the Pharisees said to Him, “Look, why are they doing what is unlawful on the Sabbath?”
units.rightText: And the Pharisees said unto him, Behold, why do they on the sabbath day that which is not lawful?

units.leftText: Jesus replied, “Have you never read what David did when he and his companions were hungry and in need?
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Did ye never read what David did, when he had need, and was hungry, he, and they that were with him?

units.leftText: During the high priesthood of Abiathar, he entered the house of God and ate the consecrated bread, which was lawful only for the priests. And he gave some to his companions as well.”
units.rightText: How he entered into the house of God when Abiathar was high priest, and ate the showbread, which it is not lawful to eat save for the priests, and gave also to them that were with him?
leftNotes: 2:26 Or the Bread of the Presence

units.leftText: Then Jesus declared, “The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath.
units.rightText: And he said unto them, The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath:

units.leftText: Therefore, the Son of Man is Lord even of the Sabbath.”
units.rightText: so that the Son of man is lord even of the sabbath.

units.leftText: Once again Jesus entered the synagogue, and a man with a withered hand was there.
units.rightText: And he entered again into the synagogue; and there was a man there who had his hand withered.

units.leftText: In order to accuse Jesus, they were watching to see if He would heal on the Sabbath.
units.rightText: And they watched him, whether he would heal him on the sabbath day; that they might accuse him.

units.leftText: Then Jesus said to the man with the withered hand, “Stand up among us.”
units.rightText: And he saith unto the man that had his hand withered, Stand forth.

units.leftText: And He asked them, “Which is lawful on the Sabbath: to do good or to do evil, to save life or to destroy it?” But they were silent.
units.rightText: And he saith unto them, Is it lawful on the sabbath day to do good, or to do harm? to save a life, or to kill? But they held their peace.

units.leftText: Jesus looked around at them with anger and sorrow at their hardness of heart. Then He said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” So he stretched it out, and it was restored.
units.rightText: And when he had looked round about on them with anger, being grieved at the hardening of their heart, he saith unto the man, Stretch forth thy hand. And he stretched it forth; and his hand was restored.

units.leftText: At this, the Pharisees went out and began plotting with the Herodians how they might kill Jesus. Jesus Heals the Multitudes (Matthew 4:23–25|MAT 4:23-25*; Luke 6:17–19|LUK 6:17-19*)
units.rightText: And the Pharisees went out, and straightway with the Herodians took counsel against him, how they might destroy him.

units.leftText: So Jesus withdrew with His disciples to the sea, accompanied by a large crowd from Galilee, Judea,
units.rightText: And Jesus with his disciples withdrew to the sea: and a great multitude from Galilee followed; and from Judæa,

units.leftText: Jerusalem, Idumea, the region beyond the Jordan, and the vicinity of Tyre and Sidon. The large crowd came to Him when they heard what great things He was doing.
units.rightText: and from Jerusalem, and from Idumæa, and beyond the Jordan, and about Tyre and Sidon, a great multitude, hearing what great things he did, came unto him.

units.leftText: Jesus asked His disciples to have a boat ready for Him so that the crowd would not crush Him.
units.rightText: And he spake to his disciples, that a little boat should wait on him because of the crowd, lest they should throng him:

units.leftText: For He had healed so many that all who had diseases were pressing forward to touch Him.
units.rightText: for he had healed many; insomuch that as many as had plagues pressed upon him that they might touch him.

units.leftText: And when the unclean spirits saw Him, they fell down before Him and cried out, “You are the Son of God!”
units.rightText: And the unclean spirits, whensoever they beheld him, fell down before him, and cried, saying, Thou art the Son of God.

units.leftText: But He warned them sternly not to make Him known. The Twelve Apostles (Matthew 10:1–4|MAT 10:1-4*; Luke 6:12–16|LUK 6:12-16*)
units.rightText: And he charged them much that they should not make him known.

units.leftText: Then Jesus went up on the mountain and called for those He wanted, and they came to Him.
units.rightText: And he goeth up into the mountain, and calleth unto him whom he himself would; and they went unto him.

units.leftText: He appointed twelve of them, whom He designated as apostles, to accompany Him, to be sent out to preach,
units.rightText: And he appointed twelve, that they might be with him, and that he might send them forth to preach,
leftNotes: 3:14 SBL and WH; ECM, SBL, NE, BYZ, and TR do not include whom He designated as apostles

units.leftText: and to have authority to drive out demons.
units.rightText: and to have authority to cast out demons:
leftNotes: 3:15 BYZ and TR include to heal sicknesses, and

units.leftText: These are the twelve He appointed: Simon (whom He named Peter),
units.rightText: and Simon he surnamed Peter;
leftNotes: 3:16 SBL, NE, and WH; ECM, BYZ, and TR do not include These are the twelve He appointed

units.leftText: James son of Zebedee and his brother John ( whom He named Boanerges, meaning “Sons of Thunder”),
units.rightText: and James the son of Zebedee, and John the brother of James; and them he surnamed Boanerges, which is, Sons of thunder:

units.leftText: Andrew, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, Simon the Zealot,
units.rightText: and Andrew, and Philip, and Bartholomew, and Matthew, and Thomas, and James the son of Alphæus, and Thaddæus, and Simon the Cananæan,
leftNotes: 3:18 Greek Simon the Cananean

units.leftText: and Judas Iscariot, who betrayed Jesus. A House Divided (Matthew 12:22–30|MAT 12:22-30*; Luke 11:14–23|LUK 11:14-23*)
units.rightText: and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him. And he cometh into a house.
leftNotes: 3:19 Literally who also betrayed Him

units.leftText: Then Jesus went home, and once again a crowd gathered, so that He and His disciples could not even eat.
units.rightText: And the multitude cometh together again, so that they could not so much as eat bread.
leftNotes: 3:20 Literally Then He comes to a house

units.leftText: When His family heard about this, they went out to take custody of Him, saying, “He is out of His mind.”
units.rightText: And when his friends heard it, they went out to lay hold on him: for they said, He is beside himself.

units.leftText: And the scribes who had come down from Jerusalem were saying, “He is possessed by Beelzebul, ” and, “By the prince of the demons He drives out demons.”
units.rightText: And the scribes that came down from Jerusalem said, He hath Beelzebub, and, By the prince of the demons casteth he out the demons.
leftNotes: 3:22 WH Beezeboul; Vulgate Beelzebub

units.leftText: So Jesus called them together and began to speak to them in parables: “How can Satan drive out Satan?
units.rightText: And he called them unto him, and said unto them in parables, How can Satan cast out Satan?

units.leftText: If a kingdom is divided against itself, it cannot stand.
units.rightText: And if a kingdom be divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand.

units.leftText: If a house is divided against itself, it cannot stand.
units.rightText: And if a house be divided against itself, that house will not be able to stand.

units.leftText: And if Satan is divided and rises against himself, he cannot stand; his end has come.
units.rightText: And if Satan hath risen up against himself, and is divided, he cannot stand, but hath an end.

units.leftText: Indeed, no one can enter a strong man’s house to steal his possessions unless he first ties up the strong man. Then he can plunder his house. The Unpardonable Sin (Matthew 12:31–32|MAT 12:31-32*)
units.rightText: But no one can enter into the house of the strong man, and spoil his goods, except he first bind the strong man; and then he will spoil his house.

units.leftText: Truly I tell you, the sons of men will be forgiven all sins and blasphemies, as many as they utter.
units.rightText: Verily I say unto you, All their sins shall be forgiven unto the sons of men, and their blasphemies wherewith soever they shall blaspheme:

units.leftText: But whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will never be forgiven; he is guilty of eternal sin.”
units.rightText: but whosoever shall blaspheme against the Holy Spirit hath never forgiveness, but is guilty of an eternal sin:

units.leftText: Jesus made this statement because they were saying, “He has an unclean spirit.” Jesus’ Mother and Brothers (Matthew 12:46–50|MAT 12:46-50*; Luke 8:19–21|LUK 8:19-21*)
units.rightText: because they said, He hath an unclean spirit.

units.leftText: Then Jesus’ mother and brothers came and stood outside. They sent someone in to summon Him,
units.rightText: And there come his mother and his brethren; and, standing without, they sent unto him, calling him.

units.leftText: and a crowd was sitting around Him. “Look,” He was told, “Your mother and brothers are outside, asking for You.”
units.rightText: And a multitude was sitting about him; and they say unto him, Behold, thy mother and thy brethren without seek for thee.
leftNotes: 3:32 ECM, SBL, WH, and TR; NE and BYZ include and Your sisters.

units.leftText: But Jesus replied, “Who are My mother and My brothers?”
units.rightText: And he answereth them, and saith, Who is my mother and my brethren?

units.leftText: Looking at those seated in a circle around Him, He said, “Here are My mother and My brothers!
units.rightText: And looking round on them that sat round about him, he saith, Behold, my mother and my brethren!

units.leftText: For whoever does the will of God is My brother and sister and mother.”
units.rightText: For whosoever shall do the will of God, the same is my brother, and sister, and mother.

units.leftText: Once again Jesus began to teach beside the sea, and such a large crowd gathered around Him that He got into a boat and sat in it, while all the people crowded along the shore.
units.rightText: And again he began to teach by the sea side. And there is gathered unto him a very great multitude, so that he entered into a boat, and sat in the sea; and all the multitude were by the sea on the land.

units.leftText: And He taught them many things in parables, and in His teaching He said,
units.rightText: And he taught them many things in parables, and said unto them in his teaching,

units.leftText: “Listen! A farmer went out to sow his seed.
units.rightText: Hearken: Behold, the sower went forth to sow:

units.leftText: And as he was sowing, some seed fell along the path, and the birds came and devoured it.
units.rightText: and it came to pass, as he sowed, some seed fell by the way side, and the birds came and devoured it.

units.leftText: Some fell on rocky ground, where it did not have much soil. It sprang up quickly because the soil was shallow.
units.rightText: And other fell on the rocky ground, where it had not much earth; and straightway it sprang up, because it had no deepness of earth:

units.leftText: But when the sun rose, the seedlings were scorched, and they withered because they had no root.
units.rightText: and when the sun was risen, it was scorched; and because it had no root, it withered away.

units.leftText: Other seed fell among thorns, which grew up and choked the seedlings, and they yielded no crop.
units.rightText: And other fell among the thorns, and the thorns grew up, and choked it, and it yielded no fruit.

units.leftText: Still other seed fell on good soil, where it sprouted, grew up, and produced a crop — one bearing thirtyfold, another sixtyfold, and another a hundredfold.”
units.rightText: And others fell into the good ground, and yielded fruit, growing up and increasing; and brought forth, thirtyfold, and sixtyfold, and a hundredfold.

units.leftText: Then Jesus said, “He who has ears to hear, let him hear.” The Purpose of Jesus’ Parables (Isaiah 6:1–13|ISA 6:1-13*; Matthew 13:10–17|MAT 13:10-17*; Luke 8:9–10|LUK 8:9-10*)
units.rightText: And he said, Who hath ears to hear, let him hear.

units.leftText: As soon as Jesus was alone with the Twelve and those around Him, they asked Him about the parable.
units.rightText: And when he was alone, they that were about him with the twelve asked of him the parables.

units.leftText: He replied, “The mystery of the kingdom of God has been given to you, but to those on the outside everything is expressed in parables,
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Unto you is given the mystery of the kingdom of God: but unto them that are without, all things are done in parables:

units.leftText: so that, ‘they may be ever seeing but never perceiving, and ever hearing but never understanding; otherwise they might turn and be forgiven.’ ” The Parable of the Sower Explained (Matthew 13:18–23|MAT 13:18-23*; Luke 8:11–15|LUK 8:11-15*)
units.rightText: that seeing they may see, and not perceive; and hearing they may hear, and not understand; lest haply they should turn again, and it should be forgiven them.
leftNotes: 4:12 Isaiah 6:9–10|ISA 6:9-10* (see also LXX)

units.leftText: Then Jesus said to them, “Do you not understand this parable? Then how will you understand any of the parables?
units.rightText: And he saith unto them, Know ye not this parable? and how shall ye know all the parables?

units.leftText: The farmer sows the word.
units.rightText: The sower soweth the word.

units.leftText: Some are like the seeds along the path, where the word is sown. As soon as they hear it, Satan comes and takes away the word that was sown in them.
units.rightText: And these are they by the way side, where the word is sown; and when they have heard, straightway cometh Satan, and taketh away the word which hath been sown in them.
leftNotes: 4:15 Or the word; similarly in verses 16, 18, and 20; literally Now these are the ones

units.leftText: Some are like the seeds sown on rocky ground. They hear the word and at once receive it with joy.
units.rightText: And these in like manner are they that are sown upon the rocky places, who, when they have heard the word, straightway receive it with joy;

units.leftText: But they themselves have no root, and they remain for only a season. When trouble or persecution comes because of the word, they quickly fall away.
units.rightText: and they have no root in themselves, but endure for a while; then, when tribulation or persecution ariseth because of the word, straightway they stumble.

units.leftText: Others are like the seeds sown among the thorns. They hear the word,
units.rightText: And others are they that are sown among the thorns; these are they that have heard the word,

units.leftText: but the worries of this life, the deceitfulness of wealth, and the desire for other things come in and choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.
units.rightText: and the cares of the world, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things entering in, choke the word, and it becometh unfruitful.

units.leftText: Still others are like the seeds sown on good soil. They hear the word, receive it, and produce a crop — thirtyfold, sixtyfold, or a hundredfold.” The Lesson of the Lamp (Luke 8:16–18|LUK 8:16-18*)
units.rightText: And those are they that were sown upon the good ground; such as hear the word, and accept it, and bear fruit, thirtyfold, and sixtyfold, and a hundredfold.

units.leftText: Jesus also said to them, “Does anyone bring in a lamp to put it under a basket or under a bed? Doesn’t he set it on a stand?
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Is the lamp brought to be put under the bushel, or under the bed, and not to be put on the stand?

units.leftText: For there is nothing hidden that will not be disclosed, and nothing concealed that will not be brought to light.
units.rightText: For there is nothing hid, save that it should be manifested; neither was anything made secret, but that it should come to light.

units.leftText: If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear.”
units.rightText: If any man hath ears to hear, let him hear.

units.leftText: He went on to say, “Pay attention to what you hear. With the measure you use, it will be measured to you, and even more will be added to you.
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Take heed what ye hear: with what measure ye mete it shall be measured unto you; and more shall be given unto you.

units.leftText: For whoever has will be given more. But whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.” The Seed Growing Secretly
units.rightText: For he that hath, to him shall be given: and he that hath not, from him shall be taken away even that which he hath.

units.leftText: Jesus also said, “The kingdom of God is like a man who scatters seed on the ground.
units.rightText: And he said, So is the kingdom of God, as if a man should cast seed upon the earth;

units.leftText: Night and day he sleeps and wakes, and the seed sprouts and grows, though he knows not how.
units.rightText: and should sleep and rise night and day, and the seed should spring up and grow, he knoweth not how.

units.leftText: All by itself the earth produces a crop— first the stalk, then the head, then grain that ripens within.
units.rightText: The earth beareth fruit of herself; first the blade, then the ear, then the full grain in the ear.

units.leftText: And as soon as the grain is ripe, he swings the sickle, because the harvest has come. ” The Parable of the Mustard Seed (Matthew 13:31–32|MAT 13:31-32*; Luke 13:18–19|LUK 13:18-19*)
units.rightText: But when the fruit is ripe, straightway he putteth forth the sickle, because the harvest is come.
leftNotes: 4:29 See Joel 3:13|JOL 3:13*, including LXX.

units.leftText: Then He asked, “To what can we compare the kingdom of God? With what parable shall we present it?
units.rightText: And he said, How shall we liken the kingdom of God? or in what parable shall we set it forth?

units.leftText: It is like a mustard seed, which is the smallest of all seeds sown upon the earth.
units.rightText: It is like a grain of mustard seed, which, when it is sown upon the earth, though it be less than all the seeds that are upon the earth,

units.leftText: But after it is planted, it grows to be the largest of all garden plants and puts forth great branches, so that the birds of the air nest in its shade.”
units.rightText: yet when it is sown, groweth up, and becometh greater than all the herbs, and putteth out great branches; so that the birds of the heaven can lodge under the shadow thereof.

units.leftText: With many such parables Jesus spoke the word to them, to the extent that they could understand.
units.rightText: And with many such parables spake he the word unto them, as they were able to hear it;

units.leftText: He did not tell them anything without using a parable. But privately He explained everything to His own disciples. Jesus Calms the Storm (Psalm 107:1–43|PSA 107:1-43*; Matthew 8:23–27|MAT 8:23-27*; Luke 8:22–25|LUK 8:22-25*)
units.rightText: and without a parable spake he not unto them: but privately to his own disciples he expounded all things.

units.leftText: When that evening came, He said to His disciples, “Let us cross to the other side.”
units.rightText: And on that day, when even was come, he saith unto them, Let us go over unto the other side.

units.leftText: After they had dismissed the crowd, they took Jesus with them, since He was already in the boat. And there were other boats with Him.
units.rightText: And leaving the multitude, they take him with them, even as he was, in the boat. And other boats were with him.

units.leftText: Soon a violent windstorm came up, and the waves were breaking over the boat, so that it was being swamped.
units.rightText: And there ariseth a great storm of wind, and the waves beat into the boat, insomuch that the boat was now filling.

units.leftText: But Jesus was in the stern, sleeping on the cushion. So they woke Him and said, “Teacher, don’t You care that we are perishing?”
units.rightText: And he himself was in the stern, asleep on the cushion: and they awake him, and say unto him, Teacher, carest thou not that we perish?

units.leftText: Then Jesus got up and rebuked the wind and the sea. “Silence!” He commanded. “Be still!” And the wind died down, and it was perfectly calm.
units.rightText: And he awoke, and rebuked the wind, and said unto the sea, Peace, be still. And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm.

units.leftText: “Why are you so afraid?” He asked. “Do you still have no faith?”
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Why are ye fearful? have ye not yet faith?

units.leftText: Overwhelmed with fear, they asked one another, “Who is this, that even the wind and the sea obey Him?”
units.rightText: And they feared exceedingly, and said one to another, Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?

units.leftText: On the other side of the sea, they arrived in the region of the Gerasenes.
units.rightText: And they came to the other side of the sea, into the country of the Gerasenes.
leftNotes: 5:1 BYZ and TR Gadarenes; PT Gergesenes

units.leftText: As soon as Jesus got out of the boat, He was met by a man with an unclean spirit, who was coming from the tombs.
units.rightText: And when he was come out of the boat, straightway there met him out of the tombs a man with an unclean spirit,

units.leftText: This man had been living in the tombs and could no longer be restrained, even with chains.
units.rightText: who had his dwelling in the tombs: and no man could any more bind him, no, not with a chain;

units.leftText: Though he was often bound with chains and shackles, he had broken the chains and shattered the shackles. Now there was no one with the strength to subdue him.
units.rightText: because that he had been often bound with fetters and chains, and the chains had been rent asunder by him, and the fetters broken in pieces: and no man had strength to tame him.

units.leftText: Night and day in the tombs and in the mountains he kept crying out and cutting himself with stones.
units.rightText: And always, night and day, in the tombs and in the mountains, he was crying out, and cutting himself with stones.

units.leftText: When the man saw Jesus from a distance, he ran and fell on his knees before Him.
units.rightText: And when he saw Jesus from afar, he ran and worshipped him;

units.leftText: And he shouted in a loud voice, “What do You want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I beg You before God not to torture me!”
units.rightText: and crying out with a loud voice, he saith, What have I to do with thee, Jesus, thou Son of the Most High God? I adjure thee by God, torment me not.

units.leftText: For Jesus had already declared, “Come out of this man, you unclean spirit!”
units.rightText: For he said unto him, Come forth, thou unclean spirit, out of the man.

units.leftText: “What is your name?” Jesus asked.
units.rightText: And he asked him, What is thy name? And he saith unto him, My name is Legion; for we are many.

units.leftText: And he begged Jesus repeatedly not to send them out of that region.
units.rightText: And he besought him much that he would not send them away out of the country.

units.leftText: There on the nearby hillside a large herd of pigs was feeding.
units.rightText: Now there was there on the mountain side a great herd of swine feeding.

units.leftText: So the demons begged Jesus, “Send us to the pigs, so that we may enter them.”
units.rightText: And they besought him, saying, Send us into the swine, that we may enter into them.

units.leftText: He gave them permission, and the unclean spirits came out and went into the pigs, and the herd of about two thousand rushed down the steep bank into the sea and drowned in the water.
units.rightText: And he gave them leave. And the unclean spirits came out, and entered into the swine: and the herd rushed down the steep into the sea, in number about two thousand; and they were drowned in the sea.
leftNotes: 5:13 Literally and were drowned in the sea

units.leftText: Those tending the pigs ran off and reported this in the town and countryside, and the people went out to see what had happened.
units.rightText: And they that fed them fled, and told it in the city, and in the country. And they came to see what it was that had come to pass.

units.leftText: When they came to Jesus, they saw the man who had been possessed by the legion of demons sitting there, clothed and in his right mind; and they were afraid.
units.rightText: And they come to Jesus, and behold him that was possessed with demons sitting, clothed and in his right mind, even him that had the legion: and they were afraid.

units.leftText: Those who had seen it described what had happened to the demon-possessed man and also to the pigs.
units.rightText: And they that saw it declared unto them how it befell him that was possessed with demons, and concerning the swine.

units.leftText: And the people began to beg Jesus to leave their region.
units.rightText: And they began to beseech him to depart from their borders.

units.leftText: As He was getting into the boat, the man who had been possessed by the demons begged to go with Him.
units.rightText: And as he was entering into the boat, he that had been possessed with demons besought him that he might be with him.

units.leftText: But Jesus would not allow him. “Go home to your own people,” He said, “and tell them how much the Lord has done for you, and what mercy He has shown you.”
units.rightText: And he suffered him not, but saith unto him, Go to thy house unto thy friends, and tell them how great things the Lord hath done for thee, and how he had mercy on thee.

units.leftText: So the man went away and began to proclaim throughout the Decapolis how much Jesus had done for him. And everyone was amazed. The Healing Touch of Jesus (Matthew 9:18–26|MAT 9:18-26*; Luke 8:40–56|LUK 8:40-56*)
units.rightText: And he went his way, and began to publish in Decapolis how great things Jesus had done for him: and all men marvelled.
leftNotes: 5:20 That is, the Ten Cities

units.leftText: When Jesus had again crossed by boat to the other side, a large crowd gathered around Him beside the sea.
units.rightText: And when Jesus had crossed over again in the boat unto the other side, a great multitude was gathered unto him; and he was by the sea.

units.leftText: A synagogue leader named Jairus arrived, and seeing Jesus, he fell at His feet
units.rightText: And there cometh one of the rulers of the synagogue, Jaïrus by name; and seeing him, he falleth at his feet,

units.leftText: and pleaded with Him urgently, “My little daughter is near death. Please come and place Your hands on her, so that she will be healed and live.”
units.rightText: and beseecheth him much, saying, My little daughter is at the point of death: I pray thee, that thou come and lay thy hands on her, that she may be made whole, and live.

units.leftText: So Jesus went with him, and a large crowd followed and pressed around Him.
units.rightText: And he went with him; and a great multitude followed him, and they thronged him.

units.leftText: And a woman was there who had suffered from bleeding for twelve years.
units.rightText: And a woman, who had an issue of blood twelve years,

units.leftText: She had borne much agony under the care of many physicians and had spent all she had, but to no avail. Instead, her condition had only grown worse.
units.rightText: and had suffered many things of many physicians, and had spent all that she had, and was nothing bettered, but rather grew worse,

units.leftText: When the woman heard about Jesus, she came up through the crowd behind Him and touched His cloak.
units.rightText: having heard the things concerning Jesus, came in the crowd behind, and touched his garment.

units.leftText: For she kept saying, “If only I touch His garments, I will be healed.”
units.rightText: For she said, If I touch but his garments, I shall be made whole.

units.leftText: Immediately her bleeding stopped, and she sensed in her body that she was healed of her affliction.
units.rightText: And straightway the fountain of her blood was dried up; and she felt in her body that she was healed of her plague.

units.leftText: At once Jesus was aware that power had gone out from Him. Turning to the crowd, He asked, “Who touched My garments?”
units.rightText: And straightway Jesus, perceiving in himself that the power proceeding from him had gone forth, turned him about in the crowd, and said, Who touched my garments?

units.leftText: His disciples answered, “You can see the crowd pressing in on You, and yet You ask, ‘Who touched Me?’”
units.rightText: And his disciples said unto him, Thou seest the multitude thronging thee, and sayest thou, Who touched me?

units.leftText: But He kept looking around to see who had done this.
units.rightText: And he looked round about to see her that had done this thing.

units.leftText: Then the woman, knowing what had happened to her, came and fell down before Him trembling in fear, and she told Him the whole truth.
units.rightText: But the woman fearing and trembling, knowing what had been done to her, came and fell down before him, and told him all the truth.

units.leftText: “Daughter,” said Jesus, “your faith has healed you. Go in peace and be free of your affliction.”
units.rightText: And he said unto her, Daughter, thy faith hath made thee whole; go in peace, and be whole of thy plague.

units.leftText: While He was still speaking, messengers from the house of Jairus arrived and said, “Your daughter is dead; why bother the Teacher anymore?”
units.rightText: While he yet spake, they come from the ruler of the synagogue’s house, saying, Thy daughter is dead: why troublest thou the Teacher any further?

units.leftText: But Jesus overheard their conversation and said to Jairus, “Do not be afraid; just believe.”
units.rightText: But Jesus, not heeding the word spoken, saith unto the ruler of the synagogue, Fear not, only believe.
leftNotes: 5:36 Or ignored

units.leftText: And He did not allow anyone to accompany Him except Peter, James, and John the brother of James.
units.rightText: And he suffered no man to follow with him, save Peter, and James, and John the brother of James.

units.leftText: When they arrived at the house of the synagogue leader, Jesus saw the commotion and the people weeping and wailing loudly.
units.rightText: And they come to the house of the ruler of the synagogue; and he beholdeth a tumult, and many weeping and wailing greatly.

units.leftText: He went inside and asked, “Why all this commotion and weeping? The child is not dead, but asleep.”
units.rightText: And when he was entered in, he saith unto them, Why make ye a tumult, and weep? the child is not dead, but sleepeth.

units.leftText: And they laughed at Him.
units.rightText: And they laughed him to scorn. But he, having put them all forth, taketh the father of the child and her mother and them that were with him, and goeth in where the child was.

units.leftText: Taking her by the hand, Jesus said, “Talitha koum!” which means, “Little girl, I say to you, get up!”
units.rightText: And taking the child by the hand, he saith unto her, Talitha cumi; which is, being interpreted, Damsel, I say unto thee, Arise.

units.leftText: Immediately the girl got up and began to walk around (she was twelve years old). And at once they were utterly astounded.
units.rightText: And straightway the damsel rose up, and walked; for she was twelve years old. And they were amazed straightway with a great amazement.

units.leftText: Then Jesus gave strict orders that no one should know about this, and He told them to give her something to eat.
units.rightText: And he charged them much that no man should know this: and he commanded that something should be given her to eat.

units.leftText: Jesus went on from there and came to His hometown, accompanied by His disciples.
units.rightText: And he went out from thence; and he cometh into his own country; and his disciples follow him.

units.leftText: When the Sabbath came, He began to teach in the synagogue, and many who heard Him were astonished. “Where did this man get these ideas?” they asked. “What is this wisdom He has been given? And how can He perform such miracles?
units.rightText: And when the sabbath was come, he began to teach in the synagogue: and many hearing him were astonished, saying, Whence hath this man these things? and, What is the wisdom that is given unto this man, and what mean such mighty works wrought by his hands?

units.leftText: Isn’t this the carpenter, the son of Mary and the brother of James, Joses, Judas, and Simon? Aren’t His sisters here with us as well?” And they took offense at Him.
units.rightText: Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary, and brother of James, and Joses, and Judas, and Simon? and are not his sisters here with us? And they were offended in him.
leftNotes: 6:3 Joses is a variant of Joseph; see Matthew 13:55|MAT 13:55*.

units.leftText: Then Jesus said to them, “Only in his hometown, among his relatives, and in his own household is a prophet without honor.”
units.rightText: And Jesus said unto them, A prophet is not without honor, save in his own country, and among his own kin, and in his own house.

units.leftText: So He could not perform any miracles there, except to lay His hands on a few of the sick and heal them.
units.rightText: And he could there do no mighty work, save that he laid his hands upon a few sick folk, and healed them.

units.leftText: And He was amazed at their unbelief. And He went around from village to village, teaching the people. The Ministry of the Twelve (Matthew 10:5–15|MAT 10:5-15*; Luke 9:1–6|LUK 9:1-6*)
units.rightText: And he marvelled because of their unbelief. And he went round about the villages teaching.

units.leftText: Then Jesus called the Twelve to Him and began to send them out two by two, giving them authority over unclean spirits.
units.rightText: And he calleth unto him the twelve, and began to send them forth by two and two; and he gave them authority over the unclean spirits;

units.leftText: He instructed them to take nothing but a staff for the journey — no bread, no bag, no money in their belts —
units.rightText: and he charged them that they should take nothing for their journey, save a staff only; no bread, no wallet, no money in their purse;
leftNotes: 6:8 Or copper coins

units.leftText: and to wear sandals, but not a second tunic.
units.rightText: but to go shod with sandals: and, said he, put not on two coats.

units.leftText: And He told them, “When you enter a house, stay there until you leave that area.
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Wheresoever ye enter into a house, there abide till ye depart thence.

units.leftText: If anyone will not welcome you or listen to you, shake the dust off your feet when you leave that place, as a testimony against them.”
units.rightText: And whatsoever place shall not receive you, and they hear you not, as ye go forth thence, shake off the dust that is under your feet for a testimony unto them.
leftNotes: 6:11 BYZ and TR include Truly I tell you, it will be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrah on the day of judgment than for that town; see Matthew 10:15|MAT 10:15*.

units.leftText: So they set out and preached that the people should repent.
units.rightText: And they went out, and preached that men should repent.

units.leftText: They also drove out many demons and healed many of the sick, anointing them with oil. The Beheading of John (Matthew 14:1–12|MAT 14:1-12*; Luke 9:7–9|LUK 9:7-9*)
units.rightText: And they cast out many demons, and anointed with oil many that were sick, and healed them.

units.leftText: Now King Herod heard about this, for Jesus’ name had become well known, and people were saying, “John the Baptist has risen from the dead! That is why miraculous powers are at work in him.”
units.rightText: And king Herod heard thereof; for his name had become known: and he said, John the Baptizer is risen from the dead, and therefore do these powers work in him.
leftNotes: 6:14 Literally they were saying; some manuscripts he was saying

units.leftText: Others were saying, “He is Elijah,” and still others, “He is a prophet, like one of the prophets of old.”
units.rightText: But others said, It is Elijah. And others said, It is a prophet, even as one of the prophets.

units.leftText: But when Herod heard this, he said, “John, whom I beheaded, has risen from the dead!”
units.rightText: But Herod, when he heard thereof, said, John, whom I beheaded, he is risen.

units.leftText: For Herod himself had ordered that John be arrested and bound and imprisoned, on account of his brother Philip’s wife Herodias, whom Herod had married.
units.rightText: For Herod himself had sent forth and laid hold upon John, and bound him in prison for the sake of Herodias, his brother Philip’s wife; for he had married her.

units.leftText: For John had been telling Herod, “It is not lawful for you to have your brother’s wife!”
units.rightText: For John said unto Herod, It is not lawful for thee to have thy brother’s wife.

units.leftText: So Herodias held a grudge against John and wanted to kill him. But she had been unable,
units.rightText: And Herodias set herself against him, and desired to kill him; and she could not;

units.leftText: because Herod feared John and protected him, knowing that he was a righteous and holy man. When he heard John’s words, he was greatly perplexed; yet he listened to him gladly.
units.rightText: for Herod feared John, knowing that he was a righteous and holy man, and kept him safe. And when he heard him, he was much perplexed; and he heard him gladly.

units.leftText: On Herod’s birthday, her opportunity arose. Herod held a banquet for his nobles and military commanders and the leading men of Galilee.
units.rightText: And when a convenient day was come, that Herod on his birthday made a supper to his lords, and the high captains, and the chief men of Galilee;

units.leftText: When the daughter of Herodias came and danced, she pleased Herod and his guests, and the king said to the girl, “Ask me for whatever you wish, and I will give it to you.”
units.rightText: and when the daughter of Herodias herself came in and danced, she pleased Herod and them that sat at meat with him; and the king said unto the damsel, Ask of me whatsoever thou wilt, and I will give it thee.
leftNotes: 6:22 Some early manuscripts When his daughter Herodias

units.leftText: And he swore to her, “Whatever you ask of me, I will give you, up to half my kingdom!”
units.rightText: And he sware unto her, Whatsoever thou shalt ask of me, I will give it thee, unto the half of my kingdom.

units.leftText: Then she went out and asked her mother, “What should I request?” And her mother answered, “The head of John the Baptist.”
units.rightText: And she went out, and said unto her mother, What shall I ask? And she said, The head of John the Baptizer.

units.leftText: At once the girl hurried back to the king with her request: “I want you to give me the head of John the Baptist on a platter immediately.”
units.rightText: And she came in straightway with haste unto the king, and asked, saying, I will that thou forthwith give me on a platter the head of John the Baptist.

units.leftText: The king was consumed with sorrow, but because of his oaths and his guests, he did not want to refuse her.
units.rightText: And the king was exceeding sorry; but for the sake of his oaths, and of them that sat at meat, he would not reject her.

units.leftText: So without delay, the king commanded that John’s head be brought in. He sent an executioner, who went and beheaded him in the prison.
units.rightText: And straightway the king sent forth a soldier of his guard, and commanded to bring his head: and he went and beheaded him in the prison,

units.leftText: The man brought John’s head on a platter and presented it to the girl, who gave it to her mother.
units.rightText: and brought his head on a platter, and gave it to the damsel; and the damsel gave it to her mother.

units.leftText: When John’s disciples heard about this, they came and took his body and placed it in a tomb. The Feeding of the Five Thousand (Matthew 14:13–21|MAT 14:13-21*; Luke 9:10–17|LUK 9:10-17*; John 6:1–15|JHN 6:1-15*)
units.rightText: And when his disciples heard thereof, they came and took up his corpse, and laid it in a tomb.

units.leftText: Meanwhile, the apostles gathered around Jesus and brought Him news of all they had done and taught.
units.rightText: And the apostles gather themselves together unto Jesus; and they told him all things, whatsoever they had done, and whatsoever they had taught.

units.leftText: And He said to them, “Come with Me privately to a solitary place, and let us rest for a while.” For many people were coming and going, and they did not even have time to eat.
units.rightText: And he saith unto them, Come ye yourselves apart into a desert place, and rest a while. For there were many coming and going, and they had no leisure so much as to eat.

units.leftText: So they went away in a boat by themselves to a solitary place.
units.rightText: And they went away in the boat to a desert place apart.

units.leftText: But many people saw them leaving and recognized them. They ran together on foot from all the towns and arrived before them.
units.rightText: And the people saw them going, and many knew them, and they ran together there on foot from all the cities, and outwent them.

units.leftText: When Jesus stepped ashore and saw a large crowd, He had compassion on them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd. And He began to teach them many things.
units.rightText: And he came forth and saw a great multitude, and he had compassion on them, because they were as sheep not having a shepherd: and he began to teach them many things.

units.leftText: By now the hour was already late. So the disciples came to Jesus and said, “This is a desolate place, and the hour is already late.
units.rightText: And when the day was now far spent, his disciples came unto him, and said, The place is desert, and the day is now far spent;

units.leftText: Dismiss the crowd so they can go to the surrounding countryside and villages and buy themselves something to eat.”
units.rightText: send them away, that they may go into the country and villages round about, and buy themselves somewhat to eat.

units.leftText: But Jesus told them, “You give them something to eat.” They asked Him, “Should we go out and spend two hundred denarii to give all of them bread to eat?”
units.rightText: But he answered and said unto them, Give ye them to eat. And they say unto him, Shall we go and buy two hundred shillings’ worth of bread, and give them to eat?
leftNotes: 6:37 A denarius was customarily a day’s wage for a laborer; see Matthew 20:2|MAT 20:2*.

units.leftText: “Go and see how many loaves you have,” He told them. And after checking, they said, “Five — and two fish.”
units.rightText: And he saith unto them, How many loaves have ye? go and see. And when they knew, they say, Five, and two fishes.

units.leftText: Then Jesus directed them to have the people sit in groups on the green grass.
units.rightText: And he commanded them that all should sit down by companies upon the green grass.

units.leftText: So they sat down in groups of hundreds and fifties.
units.rightText: And they sat down in ranks, by hundreds, and by fifties.

units.leftText: Taking the five loaves and the two fish and looking up to heaven, Jesus spoke a blessing and broke the loaves. Then He gave them to His disciples to set before the people. And He divided the two fish among them all.
units.rightText: And he took the five loaves and the two fishes, and looking up to heaven, he blessed, and brake the loaves; and he gave to the disciples to set before them; and the two fishes divided he among them all.

units.leftText: They all ate and were satisfied,
units.rightText: And they all ate, and were filled.

units.leftText: and the disciples picked up twelve basketfuls of broken pieces of bread and fish.
units.rightText: And they took up broken pieces, twelve basketfuls, and also of the fishes.

units.leftText: And there were five thousand men who had eaten the loaves. Jesus Walks on Water (Matthew 14:22–33|MAT 14:22-33*; John 6:16–21|JHN 6:16-21*)
units.rightText: And they that ate the loaves were five thousand men.

units.leftText: Immediately Jesus made His disciples get into the boat and go on ahead of Him to Bethsaida, while He dismissed the crowd.
units.rightText: And straightway he constrained his disciples to enter into the boat, and to go before him unto the other side to Bethsaida, while he himself sendeth the multitude away.

units.leftText: After bidding them farewell, He went up on the mountain to pray.
units.rightText: And after he had taken leave of them, he departed into the mountain to pray.

units.leftText: When evening came, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and Jesus was alone on land.
units.rightText: And when even was come, the boat was in the midst of the sea, and he alone on the land.

units.leftText: He could see that the disciples were straining to row, because the wind was against them. About the fourth watch of the night, Jesus went out to them, walking on the sea. He intended to pass by them,
units.rightText: And seeing them distressed in rowing, for the wind was contrary unto them, about the fourth watch of the night he cometh unto them, walking on the sea; and he would have passed by them:
leftNotes: 6:48 That is, between three and six in the morning

units.leftText: but when they saw Him walking on the sea, they cried out, thinking He was a ghost —
units.rightText: but they, when they saw him walking on the sea, supposed that it was a ghost, and cried out;

units.leftText: for they all saw Him and were terrified.
units.rightText: for they all saw him, and were troubled. But he straightway spake with them, and saith unto them, Be of good cheer: it is I; be not afraid.

units.leftText: Then He climbed into the boat with them, and the wind died down. And the disciples were utterly astounded,
units.rightText: And he went up unto them into the boat; and the wind ceased: and they were sore amazed in themselves;

units.leftText: for they had not understood about the loaves, but their hearts had been hardened. Jesus Heals at Gennesaret (Matthew 14:34–36|MAT 14:34-36*)
units.rightText: for they understood not concerning the loaves, but their heart was hardened.

units.leftText: When they had crossed over, they landed at Gennesaret and moored the boat.
units.rightText: And when they had crossed over, they came to the land unto Gennesaret, and moored to the shore.

units.leftText: As soon as they got out of the boat, the people recognized Jesus
units.rightText: And when they were come out of the boat, straightway the people knew him,

units.leftText: and ran through that whole region, carrying the sick on mats to wherever they heard He was.
units.rightText: and ran round about that whole region, and began to carry about on their beds those that were sick, where they heard he was.

units.leftText: And wherever He went — villages and towns and countrysides — they laid the sick in the marketplaces and begged Him just to let them touch the fringe of His cloak. And all who touched Him were healed.
units.rightText: And wheresoever he entered, into villages, or into cities, or into the country, they laid the sick in the marketplaces, and besought him that they might touch if it were but the border of his garment: and as many as touched him were made whole.

units.leftText: Then the Pharisees and some of the scribes who had come from Jerusalem gathered around Jesus,
units.rightText: And there are gathered together unto him the Pharisees, and certain of the scribes, who had come from Jerusalem,

units.leftText: and they saw some of His disciples eating with hands that were defiled— that is, unwashed.
units.rightText: and had seen that some of his disciples ate their bread with defiled, that is, unwashen, hands.

units.leftText: Now in holding to the tradition of the elders, the Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat until they wash their hands ceremonially.
units.rightText: (For the Pharisees, and all the Jews, except they wash their hands diligently, eat not, holding the tradition of the elders;
leftNotes: 7:3 Literally until they have washed their hands to the fist

units.leftText: And on returning from the market, they do not eat unless they wash. And there are many other traditions for them to observe, including the washing of cups, pitchers, kettles, and couches for dining.
units.rightText: and when they come from the marketplace, except they bathe themselves, they eat not; and many other things there are, which they have received to hold, washings of cups, and pots, and brasen vessels.)
leftNotes: 7:4 NE and WH cups, pitchers, and kettles.

units.leftText: So the Pharisees and scribes questioned Jesus: “Why do Your disciples not walk according to the tradition of the elders? Instead, they eat with defiled hands.”
units.rightText: And the Pharisees and the scribes ask him, Why walk not thy disciples according to the tradition of the elders, but eat their bread with defiled hands?

units.leftText: Jesus answered them, “Isaiah prophesied correctly about you hypocrites, as it is written: ‘These people honor Me with their lips, but their hearts are far from Me.
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Well did Isaiah prophesy of you hypocrites, as it is written, This people honoreth me with their lips, But their heart is far from me.

units.leftText: They worship Me in vain; they teach as doctrine the precepts of men.’
units.rightText: But in vain do they worship me, Teaching as their doctrines the precepts of men.
leftNotes: 7:7 Isaiah 29:13|ISA 29:13* (see also LXX)

units.leftText: You have disregarded the commandment of God to keep the tradition of men. ”
units.rightText: Ye leave the commandment of God, and hold fast the tradition of men.
leftNotes: 7:8 BYZ and TR include —washings of pots and cups and many such things like these.

units.leftText: He went on to say, “You neatly set aside the command of God to maintain your own tradition.
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Full well do ye reject the commandment of God, that ye may keep your tradition.
leftNotes: 7:9 NA establish

units.leftText: For Moses said, ‘Honor your father and your mother’ and ‘Anyone who curses his father or mother must be put to death.’
units.rightText: For Moses said, Honor thy father and thy mother; and, He that speaketh evil of father or mother, let him die the death:
leftNotes: 7:10 Exodus 20:12|EXO 20:12*; Deuteronomy 5:16
7:10 Exodus 21:17|EXO 21:17*; Leviticus 20:9

units.leftText: But you say that if a man says to his father or mother, ‘Whatever you would have received from me is Corban’ (that is, a gift devoted to God ),
units.rightText: but ye say, If a man shall say to his father or his mother, That wherewith thou mightest have been profited by me is Corban, that is to say, Given to God;

units.leftText: he is no longer permitted to do anything for his father or mother.
units.rightText: ye no longer suffer him to do aught for his father or his mother;

units.leftText: Thus you nullify the word of God by the tradition you have handed down. And you do so in many such matters.” What Defiles a Man (Matthew 15:10–20|MAT 15:10-20*)
units.rightText: making void the word of God by your tradition, which ye have delivered: and many such like things ye do.

units.leftText: Once again Jesus called the crowd to Him and said, “All of you, listen to Me and understand:
units.rightText: And he called to him the multitude again, and said unto them, Hear me all of you, and understand:

units.leftText: Nothing that enters a man from the outside can defile him; but the things that come out of a man, these are what defile him.”
units.rightText: there is nothing from without the man, that going into him can defile him; but the things which proceed out of the man are those that defile the man.
leftNotes: 7:15 BYZ and TR include 16*If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear.

rightNotes: 7:16 Many ancient authorities insert v. 16. If any man hath ears to hear, let him hear. See Mrk 4:9,23.

units.leftText: After Jesus had left the crowd and gone into the house, His disciples inquired about the parable.
units.rightText: And when he was entered into the house from the multitude, his disciples asked of him the parable.

units.leftText: “Are you still so dull?” He asked. “Do you not understand? Nothing that enters a man from the outside can defile him,
units.rightText: And he saith unto them, Are ye so without understanding also? Perceive ye not, that whatsoever from without goeth into the man, it cannot defile him;

units.leftText: because it does not enter his heart, but it goes into the stomach and then is eliminated.” (Thus all foods are clean.)
units.rightText: because it goeth not into his heart, but into his belly, and goeth out into the draught? This he said, making all meats clean.
leftNotes: 7:19 Or and then is eliminated, thereby expelling all foods.”

units.leftText: He continued: “What comes out of a man, that is what defiles him.
units.rightText: And he said, That which proceedeth out of the man, that defileth the man.

units.leftText: For from within the hearts of men come evil thoughts, sexual immorality, theft, murder, adultery,
units.rightText: For from within, out of the heart of men, evil thoughts proceed, fornications, thefts, murders, adulteries,
leftNotes: 7:21 Many texts move adultery to verse 22.

units.leftText: greed, wickedness, deceit, debauchery, envy, slander, arrogance, and foolishness.
units.rightText: covetings, wickednesses, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, railing, pride, foolishness:

units.leftText: All these evils come from within, and these are what defile a man.” The Faith of the Gentile Woman (Matthew 15:21–28|MAT 15:21-28*)
units.rightText: all these evil things proceed from within, and defile the man.

units.leftText: Jesus left that place and went to the region of Tyre. Not wanting anyone to know He was there, He entered a house, but was unable to escape their notice.
units.rightText: And from thence he arose, and went away into the borders of Tyre and Sidon. And he entered into a house, and would have no man know it; and he could not be hid.
leftNotes: 7:24 WH, BYZ, and TR include and Sidon; see Matthew 15:21|MAT 15:21*.

units.leftText: Instead, a woman whose little daughter had an unclean spirit soon heard about Jesus, and she came and fell at His feet.
units.rightText: But straightway a woman, whose little daughter had an unclean spirit, having heard of him, came and fell down at his feet.

units.leftText: Now she was a Greek woman of Syrophoenician origin, and she kept asking Jesus to drive the demon out of her daughter.
units.rightText: Now the woman was a Greek, a Syrophoenician by race. And she besought him that he would cast forth the demon out of her daughter.

units.leftText: “First let the children have their fill,” He said. “For it is not right to take the children’s bread and toss it to the dogs.”
units.rightText: And he said unto her, Let the children first be filled: for it is not meet to take the children’s bread and cast it to the dogs.

units.leftText: “Yes, Lord,” she replied, “even the dogs under the table eat the children’s crumbs.”
units.rightText: But she answered and saith unto him, Yea, Lord; even the dogs under the table eat of the children’s crumbs.
leftNotes: 7:28 Or puppies

units.leftText: Then Jesus told her, “Because of this answer, you may go. The demon has left your daughter.”
units.rightText: And he said unto her, For this saying go thy way; the demon is gone out of thy daughter.

units.leftText: And she went home and found her child lying on the bed, and the demon was gone. The Deaf and Mute Man (Matthew 9:27–34|MAT 9:27-34*)
units.rightText: And she went away unto her house, and found the child laid upon the bed, and the demon gone out.

units.leftText: Then Jesus left the region of Tyre and went through Sidon to the Sea of Galilee and into the region of the Decapolis.
units.rightText: And again he went out from the borders of Tyre, and came through Sidon unto the sea of Galilee, through the midst of the borders of Decapolis.
leftNotes: 7:31 That is, the Ten Cities

units.leftText: Some people brought to Him a man who was deaf and hardly able to speak, and they begged Jesus to place His hand on him.
units.rightText: And they bring unto him one that was deaf, and had an impediment in his speech; and they beseech him to lay his hand upon him.

units.leftText: So Jesus took him aside privately, away from the crowd, and put His fingers into the man’s ears. Then He spit and touched the man’s tongue.
units.rightText: And he took him aside from the multitude privately, and put his fingers into his ears, and he spat, and touched his tongue;

units.leftText: And looking up to heaven, He sighed deeply and said to him, “Ephphatha!” (which means, “Be opened!”).
units.rightText: and looking up to heaven, he sighed, and saith unto him, Ephphatha, that is, Be opened.

units.leftText: Immediately the man’s ears were opened and his tongue was released, and he began to speak plainly.
units.rightText: And his ears were opened, and the bond of his tongue was loosed, and he spake plain.
leftNotes: 7:35 ECM, WH, and SBL do not include Immediately.

units.leftText: Jesus ordered them not to tell anyone. But the more He ordered them, the more widely they proclaimed it.
units.rightText: And he charged them that they should tell no man: but the more he charged them, so much the more a great deal they published it.

units.leftText: The people were utterly astonished and said, “He has done all things well! He makes even the deaf hear and the mute speak!”
units.rightText: And they were beyond measure astonished, saying, He hath done all things well; he maketh even the deaf to hear, and the dumb to speak.

units.leftText: In those days the crowd once again became very large, and they had nothing to eat. Jesus called the disciples to Him and said,
units.rightText: In those days, when there was again a great multitude, and they had nothing to eat, he called unto him his disciples, and saith unto them,

units.leftText: “I have compassion for this crowd, because they have already been with Me three days and have nothing to eat.
units.rightText: I have compassion on the multitude, because they continue with me now three days, and have nothing to eat:

units.leftText: If I send them home hungry, they will faint along the way. For some of them have come a great distance.”
units.rightText: and if I send them away fasting to their home, they will faint on the way; and some of them are come from far.

units.leftText: His disciples replied, “Where in this desolate place could anyone find enough bread to feed all these people?”
units.rightText: And his disciples answered him, Whence shall one be able to fill these men with bread here in a desert place?

units.leftText: “How many loaves do you have?” Jesus asked. “Seven,” they replied.
units.rightText: And he asked them, How many loaves have ye? And they said, Seven.

units.leftText: And He instructed the crowd to sit down on the ground. Then He took the seven loaves, gave thanks and broke them, and gave them to His disciples to set before the people. And they distributed them to the crowd.
units.rightText: And he commandeth the multitude to sit down on the ground: and he took the seven loaves, and having given thanks, he brake, and gave to his disciples, to set before them; and they set them before the multitude.

units.leftText: They also had a few small fish, and Jesus blessed them and ordered that these be set before them as well.
units.rightText: And they had a few small fishes: and having blessed them, he commanded to set these also before them.

units.leftText: The people ate and were satisfied, and the disciples picked up seven basketfuls of broken pieces that were left over.
