units.rightText: And they ate, and were filled: and they took up, of broken pieces that remained over, seven baskets.

units.leftText: And about four thousand men were present.
units.rightText: And they were about four thousand: and he sent them away.
leftNotes: 8:9 Menis implied here, that is, in addition to women and children; see Matthew 15:38|MAT 15:38*.

units.leftText: He immediately got into the boat with His disciples and went to the district of Dalmanutha. The Demand for a Sign (Matthew 16:1–4|MAT 16:1-4*; Luke 12:54–56|LUK 12:54-56*)
units.rightText: And straightway he entered into the boat with his disciples, and came into the parts of Dalmanutha.

units.leftText: Then the Pharisees came and began to argue with Jesus, testing Him by demanding from Him a sign from heaven.
units.rightText: And the Pharisees came forth, and began to question with him, seeking of him a sign from heaven, trying him.

units.leftText: Jesus sighed deeply in His spirit and said, “Why does this generation demand a sign? Truly I tell you, no sign will be given to this generation.”
units.rightText: And he sighed deeply in his spirit, and saith, Why doth this generation seek a sign? verily I say unto you, There shall no sign be given unto this generation.

units.leftText: And He left them, got back into the boat, and crossed to the other side. The Leaven of the Pharisees and of Herod (Matthew 16:5–12|MAT 16:5-12*; Luke 12:1–3|LUK 12:1-3*)
units.rightText: And he left them, and again entering into the boat departed to the other side.

units.leftText: Now the disciples had forgotten to take bread, except for one loaf they had with them in the boat.
units.rightText: And they forgot to take bread; and they had not in the boat with them more than one loaf.

units.leftText: “Watch out!” He cautioned them. “Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of Herod.”
units.rightText: And he charged them, saying, Take heed, beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and the leaven of Herod.

units.leftText: So they began to discuss with one another the fact that they had no bread.
units.rightText: And they reasoned one with another, saying, We have no bread.

units.leftText: Aware of their conversation, Jesus asked them, “Why are you debating about having no bread? Do you still not see or understand? Do you have such hard hearts?
units.rightText: And Jesus perceiving it saith unto them, Why reason ye, because ye have no bread? do ye not yet perceive, neither understand? have ye your heart hardened?

units.leftText: ‘Having eyes, do you not see? And having ears, do you not hear?’ And do you not remember?
units.rightText: Having eyes, see ye not? and having ears, hear ye not? and do ye not remember?
leftNotes: 8:18 See Deuteronomy 29:4|DEU 29:4*, Isaiah 42:20, Jeremiah 5:21, and Ezekiel 12:2.

units.leftText: When I broke the five loaves for the five thousand, how many basketfuls of broken pieces did you collect?” “Twelve,” they answered.
units.rightText: When I brake the five loaves among the five thousand, how many baskets full of broken pieces took ye up? They say unto him, Twelve.

units.leftText: “And when I broke the seven loaves for the four thousand, how many basketfuls of broken pieces did you collect?” “Seven,” they said.
units.rightText: And when the seven among the four thousand, how many basketfuls of broken pieces took ye up? And they say unto him, Seven.

units.leftText: Then He asked them, “Do you still not understand?” The Blind Man at Bethsaida
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Do ye not yet understand?

units.leftText: When they arrived at Bethsaida, some people brought a blind man and begged Jesus to touch him.
units.rightText: And they come unto Bethsaida. And they bring to him a blind man, and beseech him to touch him.

units.leftText: So He took the blind man by the hand and led him out of the village. Then He spit on the man’s eyes and placed His hands on him. “Can you see anything?” He asked.
units.rightText: And he took hold of the blind man by the hand, and brought him out of the village; and when he had spit on his eyes, and laid his hands upon him, he asked him, Seest thou aught?

units.leftText: The man looked up and said, “I can see the people, but they look like trees walking around.”
units.rightText: And he looked up, and said, I see men; for I behold them as trees, walking.

units.leftText: Once again Jesus placed His hands on the man’s eyes, and when he opened them his sight was restored, and he could see everything clearly.
units.rightText: Then again he laid his hands upon his eyes; and he looked stedfastly, and was restored, and saw all things clearly.

units.leftText: Jesus sent him home and said, “Do not go back into the village.” Peter’s Confession of Christ (Matthew 16:13–20|MAT 16:13-20*; Luke 9:18–20|LUK 9:18-20*; John 6:67–71|JHN 6:67-71*)
units.rightText: And he sent him away to his home, saying, Do not even enter into the village.
leftNotes: 8:26 BYZ and TR “Do not go and tell anyone in the village.”

units.leftText: Then Jesus and His disciples went on to the villages around Caesarea Philippi. On the way, He questioned His disciples: “Who do people say I am?”
units.rightText: And Jesus went forth, and his disciples, into the villages of Cæsarea Philippi: and on the way he asked his disciples, saying unto them, Who do men say that I am?

units.leftText: They replied, “Some say John the Baptist; others say Elijah; and still others, one of the prophets.”
units.rightText: And they told him, saying, John the Baptist; and others, Elijah; but others, One of the prophets.

units.leftText: “But what about you?” Jesus asked. “Who do you say I am?” Peter answered, “You are the Christ.”
units.rightText: And he asked them, But who say ye that I am? Peter answereth and saith unto him, Thou art the Christ.

units.leftText: And Jesus warned them not to tell anyone about Him. Christ’s Passion Foretold (Matthew 16:21–23|MAT 16:21-23*; Luke 9:21–22|LUK 9:21-22*)
units.rightText: And he charged them that they should tell no man of him.

units.leftText: Then He began to teach them that the Son of Man must suffer many things and be rejected by the elders, chief priests, and scribes, and that He must be killed and after three days rise again.
units.rightText: And he began to teach them, that the Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected by the elders, and the chief priests, and the scribes, and be killed, and after three days rise again.

units.leftText: He spoke this message quite frankly, and Peter took Him aside and began to rebuke Him.
units.rightText: And he spake the saying openly. And Peter took him, and began to rebuke him.

units.leftText: But Jesus, turning and looking at His disciples, rebuked Peter and said, “Get behind Me, Satan! For you do not have in mind the things of God, but the things of men.” Take Up Your Cross (Matthew 16:24–28|MAT 16:24-28*; Luke 9:23–27|LUK 9:23-27*)
units.rightText: But he turning about, and seeing his disciples, rebuked Peter, and saith, Get thee behind me, Satan; for thou mindest not the things of God, but the things of men.

units.leftText: Then Jesus called the crowd to Him along with His disciples, and He told them, “If anyone wants to come after Me, he must deny himself and take up his cross and follow Me.
units.rightText: And he called unto him the multitude with his disciples, and said unto them, If any man would come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.

units.leftText: For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for My sake and for the gospel will save it.
units.rightText: For whosoever would save his life shall lose it; and whosoever shall lose his life for my sake and the gospel’s shall save it.

units.leftText: What does it profit a man to gain the whole world, yet forfeit his soul?
units.rightText: For what doth it profit a man, to gain the whole world, and forfeit his life?

units.leftText: Or what can a man give in exchange for his soul?
units.rightText: For what should a man give in exchange for his life?

units.leftText: If anyone is ashamed of Me and My words in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man will also be ashamed of him when He comes in His Father’s glory with the holy angels.”
units.rightText: For whosoever shall be ashamed of me and of my words in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of man also shall be ashamed of him, when he cometh in the glory of his Father with the holy angels.

units.leftText: Then Jesus said to them, “Truly I tell you, there are some standing here who will not taste death before they see the kingdom of God arrive with power.”
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Verily I say unto you, There are some here of them that stand by, who shall in no wise taste of death, till they see the kingdom of God come with power.

units.leftText: After six days Jesus took with Him Peter, James, and John, and led them up a high mountain by themselves. There He was transfigured before them.
units.rightText: And after six days Jesus taketh with him Peter, and James, and John, and bringeth them up into a high mountain apart by themselves: and he was transfigured before them;

units.leftText: His clothes became radiantly white, brighter than any launderer on earth could bleach them.
units.rightText: and his garments became glistering, exceeding white, so as no fuller on earth can whiten them.

units.leftText: And Elijah and Moses appeared before them, talking with Jesus.
units.rightText: And there appeared unto them Elijah with Moses: and they were talking with Jesus.

units.leftText: Peter said to Jesus, “Rabbi, it is good for us to be here. Let us put up three shelters — one for You, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”
units.rightText: And Peter answereth and saith to Jesus, Rabbi, it is good for us to be here: and let us make three tabernacles; one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elijah.
leftNotes: 9:5 Or three tabernacles

units.leftText: For they were all so terrified that Peter did not know what else to say.
units.rightText: For he knew not what to answer; for they became sore afraid.

units.leftText: Then a cloud appeared and enveloped them, and a voice came from the cloud: “This is My beloved Son. Listen to Him!”
units.rightText: And there came a cloud overshadowing them: and there came a voice out of the cloud, This is my beloved Son: hear ye him.

units.leftText: Suddenly, when they looked around, they saw no one with them except Jesus.
units.rightText: And suddenly looking round about, they saw no one any more, save Jesus only with themselves.

units.leftText: As they were coming down the mountain, Jesus admonished them not to tell anyone what they had seen until the Son of Man had risen from the dead.
units.rightText: And as they were coming down from the mountain, he charged them that they should tell no man what things they had seen, save when the Son of man should have risen again from the dead.

units.leftText: So they kept this matter to themselves, discussing what it meant to rise from the dead.
units.rightText: And they kept the saying, questioning among themselves what the rising again from the dead should mean.

units.leftText: And they asked Jesus, “Why do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?”
units.rightText: And they asked him, saying, How is it that the scribes say that Elijah must first come?

units.leftText: He replied, “Elijah does indeed come first, and he restores all things. Why then is it written that the Son of Man must suffer many things and be rejected?
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Elijah indeed cometh first, and restoreth all things: and how is it written of the Son of man, that he should suffer many things and be set at nought?

units.leftText: But I tell you that Elijah has indeed come, and they have done to him whatever they wished, just as it is written about him.” The Boy with an Evil Spirit (Matthew 17:14–18|MAT 17:14-18*; Luke 9:37–42|LUK 9:37-42*)
units.rightText: But I say unto you, that Elijah is come, and they have also done unto him whatsoever they would, even as it is written of him.

units.leftText: When they returned to the other disciples, they saw a large crowd around them, and scribes arguing with them.
units.rightText: And when they came to the disciples, they saw a great multitude about them, and scribes questioning with them.

units.leftText: As soon as all the people saw Jesus, they were filled with awe and ran to greet Him.
units.rightText: And straightway all the multitude, when they saw him, were greatly amazed, and running to him saluted him.

units.leftText: “What are you disputing with them?” He asked.
units.rightText: And he asked them, What question ye with them?

units.leftText: Someone in the crowd replied, “Teacher, I brought You my son, who has a spirit that makes him mute.
units.rightText: And one of the multitude answered him, Teacher, I brought unto thee my son, who hath a dumb spirit;

units.leftText: Whenever it seizes him, it throws him to the ground. He foams at the mouth, gnashes his teeth, and becomes rigid. I asked Your disciples to drive it out, but they were unable.”
units.rightText: and wheresoever it taketh him, it dasheth him down: and he foameth, and grindeth his teeth, and pineth away: and I spake to thy disciples that they should cast it out; and they were not able.
leftNotes: 9:18 Or and is withering away

units.leftText: “O unbelieving generation!” Jesus replied. “How long must I remain with you? How long must I put up with you? Bring the boy to Me.”
units.rightText: And he answereth them and saith, O faithless generation, how long shall I be with you? how long shall I bear with you? bring him unto me.

units.leftText: So they brought him, and seeing Jesus, the spirit immediately threw the boy into a convulsion. He fell to the ground and rolled around, foaming at the mouth.
units.rightText: And they brought him unto him: and when he saw him, straightway the spirit tare him grievously; and he fell on the ground, and wallowed foaming.

units.leftText: Jesus asked the boy’s father, “How long has this been with him?”
units.rightText: And he asked his father, How long time is it since this hath come unto him? And he said, From a child.

units.leftText: “It often throws him into the fire or into the water, trying to kill him. But if You can do anything, have compassion on us and help us.”
units.rightText: And oft-times it hath cast him both into the fire and into the waters, to destroy him: but if thou canst do anything, have compassion on us, and help us.

units.leftText: “If You can?” echoed Jesus. “All things are possible to him who believes!”
units.rightText: And Jesus said unto him, If thou canst! All things are possible to him that believeth.

units.leftText: Immediately the boy’s father cried out, “I do believe; help my unbelief!”
units.rightText: Straightway the father of the child cried out, and said, I believe; help thou mine unbelief.
leftNotes: 9:24 BYZ and TR cried out with tears

units.leftText: When Jesus saw that a crowd had come running, He rebuked the unclean spirit. “You deaf and mute spirit,” He said, “I command you to come out and never enter him again.”
units.rightText: And when Jesus saw that a multitude came running together, he rebuked the unclean spirit, saying unto him, Thou dumb and deaf spirit, I command thee, come out of him, and enter no more into him.

units.leftText: After shrieking and convulsing him violently, the spirit came out. The boy became like a corpse, so that many said, “He is dead.”
units.rightText: And having cried out, and torn him much, he came out: and the boy became as one dead; insomuch that the more part said, He is dead.

units.leftText: But Jesus took him by the hand and helped him to his feet, and he stood up.
units.rightText: But Jesus took him by the hand, and raised him up; and he arose.

units.leftText: After Jesus had gone into the house, His disciples asked Him privately, “Why couldn’t we drive it out?”
units.rightText: And when he was come into the house, his disciples asked him privately, How is it that we could not cast it out?

units.leftText: Jesus answered, “This kind cannot come out, except by prayer.” The Second Prediction of the Passion (Matthew 17:22–23|MAT 17:22-23*; Luke 9:43–45|LUK 9:43-45*)
units.rightText: And he said unto them, This kind can come out by nothing, save by prayer.
leftNotes: 9:29 BYZ and TR prayer and fasting

units.leftText: Going on from there, they passed through Galilee. But Jesus did not want anyone to know,
units.rightText: And they went forth from thence, and passed through Galilee; and he would not that any man should know it.

units.leftText: because He was teaching His disciples. He told them, “The Son of Man will be delivered into the hands of men. They will kill Him, and after three days He will rise.”
units.rightText: For he taught his disciples, and said unto them, The Son of man is delivered up into the hands of men, and they shall kill him; and when he is killed, after three days he shall rise again.

units.leftText: But they did not understand this statement, and they were afraid to ask Him about it. The Greatest in the Kingdom (Matthew 18:1–5|MAT 18:1-5*; Luke 9:46–50|LUK 9:46-50*)
units.rightText: But they understood not the saying, and were afraid to ask him.

units.leftText: Then they came to Capernaum. While Jesus was in the house, He asked them, “What were you discussing on the way?”
units.rightText: And they came to Capernaum: and when he was in the house he asked them, What were ye reasoning on the way?

units.leftText: But they were silent, for on the way they had been arguing about which of them was the greatest.
units.rightText: But they held their peace: for they had disputed one with another on the way, who was the greatest.

units.leftText: Sitting down, Jesus called the Twelve and said, “If anyone wants to be first, he must be the last of all and the servant of all.”
units.rightText: And he sat down, and called the twelve; and he saith unto them, If any man would be first, he shall be last of all, and servant of all.

units.leftText: Then He had a little child stand among them. Taking the child in His arms, He said to them,
units.rightText: And he took a little child, and set him in the midst of them: and taking him in his arms, he said unto them,

units.leftText: “Whoever welcomes one of these little children in My name welcomes Me, and whoever welcomes Me welcomes not only Me, but the One who sent Me.”
units.rightText: Whosoever shall receive one of such little children in my name, receiveth me: and whosoever receiveth me, receiveth not me, but him that sent me.

units.leftText: John said to Him, “Teacher, we saw someone else driving out demons in Your name, and we tried to stop him, because he does not accompany us.”
units.rightText: John said unto him, Teacher, we saw one casting out demons in thy name; and we forbade him, because he followed not us.

units.leftText: “Do not stop him,” Jesus replied. “For no one who performs a miracle in My name can turn around and speak evil of Me.
units.rightText: But Jesus said, Forbid him not: for there is no man who shall do a mighty work in my name, and be able quickly to speak evil of me.

units.leftText: For whoever is not against us is for us.
units.rightText: For he that is not against us is for us.

units.leftText: Indeed, if anyone gives you even a cup of water because you bear the name of Christ, truly I tell you, he will never lose his reward. Temptations and Trespasses (Matthew 18:6–9|MAT 18:6-9*; Luke 17:1–4|LUK 17:1-4*)
units.rightText: For whosoever shall give you a cup of water to drink, because ye are Christ’s, verily I say unto you, he shall in no wise lose his reward.

units.leftText: But if anyone causes one of these little ones who believe in Me to stumble, it would be better for him to have a large millstone hung around his neck and to be thrown into the sea.
units.rightText: And whosoever shall cause one of these little ones that believe on me to stumble, it were better for him if a great millstone were hanged about his neck, and he were cast into the sea.

units.leftText: If your hand causes you to sin, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life crippled than to have two hands and go into hell, into the unquenchable fire.
units.rightText: And if thy hand cause thee to stumble, cut it off: it is good for thee to enter into life maimed, rather than having thy two hands to go into hell, into the unquenchable fire.
leftNotes: 9:43 Greek Gehenna; also in verses 45 and 47
9:43 BYZ and TR include 44*where their worm never dies, and the fire is never quenched; see verse 48 and Isaiah 66:24|ISA 66:24*.

rightNotes: 9:44 Vs. 44 and 46 (which are identical with v. 48) are omitted by the best ancient authorities.

units.leftText: If your foot causes you to sin, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life lame than to have two feet and be thrown into hell.
units.rightText: And if thy foot cause thee to stumble, cut it off: it is good for thee to enter into life halt, rather than having thy two feet to be cast into hell.
leftNotes: 9:45 BYZ and TR include 46*where their worm never dies, and the fire is never quenched; see verse 48 and Isaiah 66:24|ISA 66:24*.

rightNotes: 9:46 Vs. 44 and 46 (which are identical with v. 48) are omitted by the best ancient authorities.

units.leftText: And if your eye causes you to sin, pluck it out. It is better for you to enter the kingdom of God with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into hell,
units.rightText: And if thine eye cause thee to stumble, cast it out: it is good for thee to enter into the kingdom of God with one eye, rather than having two eyes to be cast into hell;

units.leftText: where ‘their worm never dies, and the fire is never quenched.’ Good Salt (Matthew 5:13–16|MAT 5:13-16*; Luke 14:34–35|LUK 14:34-35*)
units.rightText: where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched.

units.leftText: For everyone will be salted with fire.
units.rightText: For every one shall be salted with fire.
leftNotes: 9:49 BYZ and TR include and every sacrifice will be salted with salt.

units.leftText: Salt is good, but if the salt loses its saltiness, with what will you season it? Have salt among yourselves, and be at peace with one another.”
units.rightText: Salt is good: but if the salt have lost its saltness, wherewith will ye season it? Have salt in yourselves, and be at peace one with another.

units.leftText: Then Jesus left that place and went into the region of Judea, beyond the Jordan. Again the crowds came to Him and He taught them, as was His custom.
units.rightText: And he arose from thence, and cometh into the borders of Judæa and beyond the Jordan: and multitudes come together unto him again; and, as he was wont, he taught them again.

units.leftText: Some Pharisees came to test Him. “Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife?” they inquired.
units.rightText: And there came unto him Pharisees, and asked him, Is it lawful for a man to put away his wife? trying him.

units.leftText: “What did Moses command you?” He replied.
units.rightText: And he answered and said unto them, What did Moses command you?

units.leftText: They answered, “Moses permitted a man to write his wife a certificate of divorce and send her away.”
units.rightText: And they said, Moses suffered to write a bill of divorcement, and to put her away.
leftNotes: 10:4 See Deuteronomy 24:1|DEU 24:1*.

units.leftText: But Jesus told them, “Moses wrote this commandment for you because of your hardness of heart.
units.rightText: But Jesus said unto them, For your hardness of heart he wrote you this commandment.

units.leftText: However, from the beginning of creation, ‘God made them male and female.’
units.rightText: But from the beginning of the creation, Male and female made he them.
leftNotes: 10:6 Genesis 1:27|GEN 1:27*; Genesis 5:2

units.leftText: ‘For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be united to his wife,
units.rightText: For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife;
leftNotes: 10:7 NE and WH do not include and be united to his wife.

units.leftText: and the two will become one flesh.’ So they are no longer two, but one flesh.
units.rightText: and the two shall become one flesh: so that they are no more two, but one flesh.
leftNotes: 10:8 Genesis 2:24|GEN 2:24* (see also LXX)

units.leftText: Therefore what God has joined together, let man not separate.”
units.rightText: What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder.

units.leftText: When they were back inside the house, the disciples asked Jesus about this matter.
units.rightText: And in the house the disciples asked him again of this matter.

units.leftText: So He told them, “Whoever divorces his wife and marries another woman commits adultery against her.
units.rightText: And he saith unto them, Whosoever shall put away his wife, and marry another, committeth adultery against her:

units.leftText: And if a woman divorces her husband and marries another man, she commits adultery.” Jesus Blesses the Children (Matthew 19:13–15|MAT 19:13-15*; Luke 18:15–17|LUK 18:15-17*)
units.rightText: and if she herself shall put away her husband, and marry another, she committeth adultery.

units.leftText: Now people were bringing the little children to Jesus for Him to place His hands on them, and the disciples rebuked those who brought them.
units.rightText: And they were bringing unto him little children, that he should touch them: and the disciples rebuked them.

units.leftText: But when Jesus saw this, He was indignant and told them, “Let the little children come to Me, and do not hinder them! For the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.
units.rightText: But when Jesus saw it, he was moved with indignation, and said unto them, Suffer the little children to come unto me; forbid them not: for to such belongeth the kingdom of God.

units.leftText: Truly I tell you, anyone who does not receive the kingdom of God like a little child will never enter it.”
units.rightText: Verily I say unto you, Whosoever shall not receive the kingdom of God as a little child, he shall in no wise enter therein.

units.leftText: And He took the children in His arms, placed His hands on them, and blessed them. The Rich Young Man (Matthew 19:16–30|MAT 19:16-30*; Luke 18:18–30|LUK 18:18-30*)
units.rightText: And he took them in his arms, and blessed them, laying his hands upon them.

units.leftText: As Jesus started on His way, a man ran up and knelt before Him. “Good Teacher,” he asked, “what must I do to inherit eternal life?”
units.rightText: And as he was going forth into the way, there ran one to him, and kneeled to him, and asked him, Good Teacher, what shall I do that I may inherit eternal life?

units.leftText: “Why do you call Me good?” Jesus replied. “No one is good except God alone.
units.rightText: And Jesus said unto him, Why callest thou me good? none is good save one, even God.

units.leftText: You know the commandments: ‘Do not murder, do not commit adultery, do not steal, do not bear false witness, do not cheat others, honor your father and mother.’ ”
units.rightText: Thou knowest the commandments, Do not kill, Do not commit adultery, Do not steal, Do not bear false witness, Do not defraud, Honor thy father and mother.

units.leftText: “Teacher,” he replied, “all these I have kept from my youth.”
units.rightText: And he said unto him, Teacher, all these things have I observed from my youth.

units.leftText: Jesus looked at him, loved him, and said to him, “There is one thing you lack: Go, sell everything you own and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow Me. ”
units.rightText: And Jesus looking upon him loved him, and said unto him, One thing thou lackest: go, sell whatsoever thou hast, and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come, follow me.
leftNotes: 10:21 BYZ and TR Then come, take up the cross, and follow Me.

units.leftText: But the man was saddened by these words and went away in sorrow, because he had great wealth.
units.rightText: But his countenance fell at the saying, and he went away sorrowful: for he was one that had great possessions.

units.leftText: Then Jesus looked around and said to His disciples, “How hard it is for the rich to enter the kingdom of God!”
units.rightText: And Jesus looked round about, and saith unto his disciples, How hardly shall they that have riches enter into the kingdom of God!

units.leftText: And the disciples were amazed at His words.
units.rightText: And the disciples were amazed at his words. But Jesus answereth again, and saith unto them, Children, how hard is it for them that trust in riches to enter into the kingdom of God!

units.leftText: It is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God.”
units.rightText: It is easier for a camel to go through a needle’s eye, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.

units.leftText: They were even more astonished and said to one another, “Who then can be saved?”
units.rightText: And they were astonished exceedingly, saying unto him, Then who can be saved?

units.leftText: Jesus looked at them and said, “With man this is impossible, but not with God. For all things are possible with God.”
units.rightText: Jesus looking upon them saith, With men it is impossible, but not with God: for all things are possible with God.

units.leftText: Peter began to say to Him, “Look, we have left everything and followed You.”
units.rightText: Peter began to say unto him, Lo, we have left all, and have followed thee.

units.leftText: “Truly I tell you,” Jesus replied, “no one who has left home or brothers or sisters or mother or father or children or fields for My sake and for the gospel
units.rightText: Jesus said, Verily I say unto you, There is no man that hath left house, or brethren, or sisters, or mother, or father, or children, or lands, for my sake, and for the gospel’s sake,

units.leftText: will fail to receive a hundredfold in the present age — houses and brothers and sisters and mothers and children and fields, along with persecutions — and in the age to come, eternal life.
units.rightText: but he shall receive a hundredfold now in this time, houses, and brethren, and sisters, and mothers, and children, and lands, with persecutions; and in the world to come eternal life.

units.leftText: But many who are first will be last, and the last will be first.” The Third Prediction of the Passion (Matthew 20:17–19|MAT 20:17-19*; Luke 18:31–34|LUK 18:31-34*)
units.rightText: But many that are first shall be last; and the last first.

units.leftText: As they were going up the road to Jerusalem, Jesus was walking ahead of them. The disciples were amazed, but those who followed were afraid. Again Jesus took the Twelve aside and began to tell them what was going to happen to Him:
units.rightText: And they were on the way, going up to Jerusalem; and Jesus was going before them: and they were amazed; and they that followed were afraid. And he took again the twelve, and began to tell them the things that were to happen unto him,

units.leftText: “Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be delivered over to the chief priests and scribes. They will condemn Him to death and will deliver Him over to the Gentiles,
units.rightText: saying, Behold, we go up to Jerusalem; and the Son of man shall be delivered unto the chief priests and the scribes; and they shall condemn him to death, and shall deliver him unto the Gentiles:

units.leftText: who will mock Him and spit on Him and flog Him and kill Him. And after three days He will rise again.” The Request of James and John (Matthew 20:20–28|MAT 20:20-28*)
units.rightText: and they shall mock him, and shall spit upon him, and shall scourge him, and shall kill him; and after three days he shall rise again.

units.leftText: Then James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came to Jesus and declared, “Teacher, we want You to do for us whatever we ask.”
units.rightText: And there come near unto him James and John, the sons of Zebedee, saying unto him, Teacher, we would that thou shouldest do for us whatsoever we shall ask of thee.

units.leftText: “What do you want Me to do for you?” He inquired.
units.rightText: And he said unto them, What would ye that I should do for you?

units.leftText: They answered, “Grant that one of us may sit at Your right hand and the other at Your left in Your glory.”
units.rightText: And they said unto him, Grant unto us that we may sit, one on thy right hand, and one on thy left hand, in thy glory.

units.leftText: “You do not know what you are asking,” Jesus replied. “Can you drink the cup I will drink, or be baptized with the baptism I will undergo?”
units.rightText: But Jesus said unto them, Ye know not what ye ask. Are ye able to drink the cup that I drink? or to be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with?

units.leftText: “We can,” the brothers answered.
units.rightText: And they said unto him, We are able. And Jesus said unto them, The cup that I drink ye shall drink; and with the baptism that I am baptized withal shall ye be baptized:

units.leftText: But to sit at My right or left is not Mine to grant. These seats belong to those for whom they have been prepared.”
units.rightText: but to sit on my right hand or on my left hand is not mine to give; but it is for them for whom it hath been prepared.
leftNotes: 10:40 Literally Mine to grant, but for whom

units.leftText: When the ten heard about this, they became indignant with James and John.
units.rightText: And when the ten heard it, they began to be moved with indignation concerning James and John.

units.leftText: So Jesus called them together and said, “You know that those regarded as rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their superiors exercise authority over them.
units.rightText: And Jesus called them to him, and saith unto them, Ye know that they who are accounted to rule over the Gentiles lord it over them; and their great ones exercise authority over them.

units.leftText: But it shall not be this way among you. Instead, whoever wants to become great among you must be your servant,
units.rightText: But it is not so among you: but whosoever would become great among you, shall be your minister;

units.leftText: and whoever wants to be first must be the slave of all.
units.rightText: and whosoever would be first among you, shall be servant of all.

units.leftText: For even the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give His life as a ransom for many.” Jesus Heals Bartimaeus (Matthew 20:29–34|MAT 20:29-34*; Luke 18:35–43|LUK 18:35-43*)
units.rightText: For the Son of man also came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many.

units.leftText: Next, they came to Jericho. And as Jesus and His disciples were leaving Jericho with a large crowd, a blind beggar named Bartimaeus, the son of Timaeus, was sitting beside the road.
units.rightText: And they come to Jericho: and as he went out from Jericho, with his disciples and a great multitude, the son of Timæus, Bartimæus, a blind beggar, was sitting by the way side.

units.leftText: When he heard that it was Jesus of Nazareth, he began to cry out, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”
units.rightText: And when he heard that it was Jesus the Nazarene, he began to cry out, and say, Jesus, thou son of David, have mercy on me.

units.leftText: Many people admonished him to be silent, but he cried out all the louder, “Son of David, have mercy on me!”
units.rightText: And many rebuked him, that he should hold his peace: but he cried out the more a great deal, Thou son of David, have mercy on me.

units.leftText: Jesus stopped and said, “Call him.” So they called the blind man. “Take courage!” they said. “Get up! He is calling for you.”
units.rightText: And Jesus stood still, and said, Call ye him. And they call the blind man, saying unto him, Be of good cheer: rise, he calleth thee.

units.leftText: Throwing off his cloak, Bartimaeus jumped up and came to Jesus.
units.rightText: And he, casting away his garment, sprang up, and came to Jesus.

units.leftText: “What do you want Me to do for you?” Jesus asked. “Rabboni,” said the blind man, “let me see again.”
units.rightText: And Jesus answered him, and said, What wilt thou that I should do unto thee? And the blind man said unto him, Rabboni, that I may receive my sight.

units.leftText: “Go,” said Jesus, “your faith has healed you.” And immediately he received his sight and followed Jesus along the road.
units.rightText: And Jesus said unto him, Go thy way; thy faith hath made thee whole. And straightway he received his sight, and followed him in the way.

units.leftText: As they approached Jerusalem and came to Bethphage and Bethany at the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent out two of His disciples
units.rightText: And when they draw nigh unto Jerusalem, unto Bethphage and Bethany, at the mount of Olives, he sendeth two of his disciples,

units.leftText: and said to them, “Go into the village ahead of you, and as soon as you enter it, you will find a colt tied there, on which no one has ever sat. Untie it and bring it here.
units.rightText: and saith unto them, Go your way into the village that is over against you: and straightway as ye enter into it, ye shall find a colt tied, whereon no man ever yet sat; loose him, and bring him.

units.leftText: If anyone asks, ‘Why are you doing this?’ tell him, ‘The Lord needs it and will return it shortly.’”
units.rightText: And if any one say unto you, Why do ye this? say ye, The Lord hath need of him; and straightway he will send him back hither.

units.leftText: So they went and found the colt outside in the street, tied at a doorway. They untied it,
units.rightText: And they went away, and found a colt tied at the door without in the open street; and they loose him.

units.leftText: and some who were standing there asked, “Why are you untying the colt?”
units.rightText: And certain of them that stood there said unto them, What do ye, loosing the colt?

units.leftText: The disciples answered as Jesus had instructed them, and the people gave them permission.
units.rightText: And they said unto them even as Jesus had said: and they let them go.

units.leftText: Then they led the colt to Jesus and threw their cloaks over it, and He sat on it.
units.rightText: And they bring the colt unto Jesus, and cast on him their garments; and he sat upon him.

units.leftText: Many in the crowd spread their cloaks on the road, while others spread branches they had cut from the fields.
units.rightText: And many spread their garments upon the way; and others branches, which they had cut from the fields.

units.leftText: The ones who went ahead and those who followed were shouting: “Hosanna!” “Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord!”
units.rightText: And they that went before, and they that followed, cried, Hosanna; Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord:
leftNotes: 11:9 Hosanna is a transliteration of the Hebrew Hosia-na, meaning Save, we pray or Save now, which became a shout of praise; see Psalm 118:25|PSA 118:25*.

units.leftText: “Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David!” “Hosanna in the highest!”
units.rightText: Blessed is the kingdom that cometh, the kingdom of our father David: Hosanna in the highest.
leftNotes: 11:10 Or “Hosanna in the highest heaven!”See Psalm 118:25|PSA 118:25* and Psalm 148:1.

units.leftText: Then Jesus entered Jerusalem and went into the temple courts. He looked around at everything, but since it was already late, He went out to Bethany with the Twelve. Jesus Curses the Fig Tree (Matthew 21:18–22|MAT 21:18-22*; Mark 11:20–25|MRK 11:20-25*)
units.rightText: And he entered into Jerusalem, into the temple; and when he had looked round about upon all things, it being now eventide, he went out unto Bethany with the twelve.
leftNotes: 11:11 Literally the temple; also in verses 15, 16, and 27

units.leftText: The next day, when they had left Bethany, Jesus was hungry.
units.rightText: And on the morrow, when they were come out from Bethany, he hungered.

units.leftText: Seeing in the distance a fig tree in leaf, He went to see if there was any fruit on it. But when He reached it, He found nothing on it except leaves, since it was not the season for figs.
units.rightText: And seeing a fig tree afar off having leaves, he came, if haply he might find anything thereon: and when he came to it, he found nothing but leaves; for it was not the season of figs.

units.leftText: Then He said to the tree, “May no one ever eat of your fruit again.” And His disciples heard this statement. Jesus Cleanses the Temple (Matthew 21:12–17|MAT 21:12-17*; Luke 19:45–48|LUK 19:45-48*; John 2:12–25|JHN 2:12-25*)
units.rightText: And he answered and said unto it, No man eat fruit from thee henceforward for ever. And his disciples heard it.

units.leftText: When they arrived in Jerusalem, Jesus entered the temple courts and began to drive out those who were buying and selling there. He overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those selling doves.
units.rightText: And they come to Jerusalem: and he entered into the temple, and began to cast out them that sold and them that bought in the temple, and overthrew the tables of the money-changers, and the seats of them that sold the doves;

units.leftText: And He would not allow anyone to carry merchandise through the temple courts.
units.rightText: and he would not suffer that any man should carry a vessel through the temple.

units.leftText: Then Jesus began to teach them, and He declared, “Is it not written: ‘My house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations’ ? But you have made it ‘a den of robbers.’ ”
units.rightText: And he taught, and said unto them, Is it not written, My house shall be called a house of prayer for all the nations? but ye have made it a den of robbers.
leftNotes: 11:17 Jeremiah 7:11|JER 7:11*

units.leftText: When the chief priests and scribes heard this, they looked for a way to kill Him. For they were afraid of Him, because the whole crowd was astonished at His teaching.
units.rightText: And the chief priests and the scribes heard it, and sought how they might destroy him: for they feared him, for all the multitude was astonished at his teaching.

units.leftText: And when evening came, Jesus and His disciples went out of the city. The Withered Fig Tree (Matthew 21:18–22|MAT 21:18-22*; Mark 11:12–14|MRK 11:12-14*)
units.rightText: And every evening he went forth out of the city.
leftNotes: 11:19 Literally they went; BYZ and TR He went

units.leftText: As they were walking back in the morning, they saw the fig tree withered from its roots.
units.rightText: And as they passed by in the morning, they saw the fig tree withered away from the roots.

units.leftText: Peter remembered it and said, “Look, Rabbi! The fig tree You cursed has withered.”
units.rightText: And Peter calling to remembrance saith unto him, Rabbi, behold, the fig tree which thou cursedst is withered away.

units.leftText: “Have faith in God,” Jesus said to them.
units.rightText: And Jesus answering saith unto them, Have faith in God.

units.leftText: “Truly I tell you that if anyone says to this mountain, ‘Be lifted up and thrown into the sea,’ and has no doubt in his heart but believes that it will happen, it will be done for him.
units.rightText: Verily I say unto you, Whosoever shall say unto this mountain, Be thou taken up and cast into the sea; and shall not doubt in his heart, but shall believe that what he saith cometh to pass; he shall have it.

units.leftText: Therefore I tell you, whatever you ask for in prayer, believe that you have received it, and it will be yours.
units.rightText: Therefore I say unto you, All things whatsoever ye pray and ask for, believe that ye receive them, and ye shall have them.

units.leftText: And when you stand to pray, if you hold anything against another, forgive it, so that your Father in heaven will forgive your trespasses as well. ” Jesus’ Authority Challenged (Matthew 21:23–27|MAT 21:23-27*; Luke 20:1–8|LUK 20:1-8*)
units.rightText: And whensoever ye stand praying, forgive, if ye have aught against any one; that your Father also who is in heaven may forgive you your trespasses.
leftNotes: 11:25 BYZ and TR include 26*But if you do not forgive, neither will your Father in heaven forgive your trespasses; see Matthew 6:15|MAT 6:15*.

rightNotes: 11:26 Many ancient authorities add v. 26 But if ye do not forgive, neither will your Father who is in heaven forgive your trespasses. Com. Mat 6:15; 18:35

units.leftText: After their return to Jerusalem, Jesus was walking in the temple courts, and the chief priests, scribes, and elders came up to Him.
units.rightText: And they come again to Jerusalem: and as he was walking in the temple, there come to him the chief priests, and the scribes, and the elders;

units.leftText: “By what authority are You doing these things?” they asked. “And who gave You the authority to do them?”
units.rightText: and they said unto him, By what authority doest thou these things? or who gave thee this authority to do these things?

units.leftText: “I will ask you one question,” Jesus replied, “and if you answer Me, I will tell you by what authority I am doing these things.
units.rightText: And Jesus said unto them, I will ask of you one question, and answer me, and I will tell you by what authority I do these things.

units.leftText: John’s baptism — was it from heaven or from men? Answer Me!”
units.rightText: The baptism of John, was it from heaven, or from men? answer me.

units.leftText: They deliberated among themselves what they should answer: “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ He will ask, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’
units.rightText: And they reasoned with themselves, saying, If we shall say, From heaven; he will say, Why then did ye not believe him?

units.leftText: But if we say, ‘From men’ ...” they were afraid of the people, for they all held that John truly was a prophet.
units.rightText: But should we say, From men—they feared the people: for all verily held John to be a prophet.

units.leftText: So they answered, “We do not know.” And Jesus replied, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I am doing these things.”
units.rightText: And they answered Jesus and say, We know not. And Jesus saith unto them, Neither tell I you by what authority I do these things.

units.leftText: Then Jesus began to speak to them in parables: “A man planted a vineyard. He put a wall around it, dug a wine vat, and built a watchtower. Then he rented it out to some tenants and went away on a journey.
units.rightText: And he began to speak unto them in parables. A man planted a vineyard, and set a hedge about it, and digged a pit for the winepress, and built a tower, and let it out to husbandmen, and went into another country.

units.leftText: At harvest time, he sent a servant to the tenants to collect his share of the fruit of the vineyard.
units.rightText: And at the season he sent to the husbandmen a servant, that he might receive from the husbandmen of the fruits of the vineyard.

units.leftText: But they seized the servant, beat him, and sent him away empty-handed.
units.rightText: And they took him, and beat him, and sent him away empty.

units.leftText: Then he sent them another servant, and they struck him over the head and treated him shamefully.
units.rightText: And again he sent unto them another servant; and him they wounded in the head, and handled shamefully.

units.leftText: He sent still another, and this one they killed. He sent many others; some they beat and others they killed.
units.rightText: And he sent another; and him they killed: and many others; beating some, and killing some.

units.leftText: Finally, having one beloved son, he sent him to them. ‘They will respect my son,’ he said.
units.rightText: He had yet one, a beloved son: he sent him last unto them, saying, They will reverence my son.

units.leftText: But the tenants said to one another, ‘This is the heir. Come, let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.’
units.rightText: But those husbandmen said among themselves, This is the heir; come, let us kill him, and the inheritance shall be ours.

units.leftText: So they seized the son, killed him, and threw him out of the vineyard.
units.rightText: And they took him, and killed him, and cast him forth out of the vineyard.

units.leftText: What then will the owner of the vineyard do? He will come and kill those tenants and give the vineyard to others.
units.rightText: What therefore will the lord of the vineyard do? he will come and destroy the husbandmen, and will give the vineyard unto others.

units.leftText: Have you never read this Scripture: ‘The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone.
units.rightText: Have ye not read even this scripture: The stone which the builders rejected, The same was made the head of the corner;

units.leftText: This is from the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes’ ?”
units.rightText: This was from the Lord, And it is marvellous in our eyes?

units.leftText: At this, the leaders sought to arrest Jesus, for they knew that He had spoken this parable against them. But fearing the crowd, they left Him and went away. Paying Taxes to Caesar (Matthew 22:15–22|MAT 22:15-22*; Luke 20:19–26|LUK 20:19-26*)
units.rightText: And they sought to lay hold on him; and they feared the multitude; for they perceived that he spake the parable against them: and they left him, and went away.
leftNotes: 12:12 Literally they sought

units.leftText: Later, they sent some of the Pharisees and Herodians to catch Jesus in His words.
units.rightText: And they send unto him certain of the Pharisees and of the Herodians, that they might catch him in talk.

units.leftText: “Teacher,” they said, “we know that You are honest and seek favor from no one. Indeed, You are impartial and teach the way of God in accordance with the truth. Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar or not? Should we pay them or not?”
units.rightText: And when they were come, they say unto him, Teacher, we know that thou art true, and carest not for any one; for thou regardest not the person of men, but of a truth teachest the way of God: Is it lawful to give tribute unto Cæsar, or not?

units.leftText: But Jesus saw through their hypocrisy and said, “Why are you testing Me? Bring Me a denarius to inspect.”
units.rightText: Shall we give, or shall we not give? But he, knowing their hypocrisy, said unto them, Why make ye trial of me? bring me a denarius, that I may see it.
leftNotes: 12:15 A denarius was customarily a day’s wage for a laborer; see Matthew 20:2|MAT 20:2*.

units.leftText: So they brought it, and He asked them, “Whose image is this? And whose inscription?” “Caesar’s,” they answered.
units.rightText: And they brought it. And he saith unto them, Whose is this image and superscription? And they said unto him, Cæsar’s.

units.leftText: Then Jesus told them, “Give to Caesar what is Caesar’s, and to God what is God’s.” And they marveled at Him. The Sadducees and the Resurrection (Matthew 22:23–33|MAT 22:23-33*; Luke 20:27–40|LUK 20:27-40*)
units.rightText: And Jesus said unto them, Render unto Cæsar the things that are Cæsar’s, and unto God the things that are God’s. And they marvelled greatly at him.

units.leftText: Then the Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to Jesus and questioned Him:
units.rightText: And there come unto him Sadducees, who say that there is no resurrection; and they asked him, saying,

units.leftText: “Teacher, Moses wrote for us that if a man’s brother dies and leaves a wife but no children, the man is to marry his brother’s widow and raise up offspring for him.
units.rightText: Teacher, Moses wrote unto us, If a man’s brother die, and leave a wife behind him, and leave no child, that his brother should take his wife, and raise up seed unto his brother.
leftNotes: 12:19 Deuteronomy 25:5|DEU 25:5*

units.leftText: Now there were seven brothers. The first one married and died, leaving no children.
units.rightText: There were seven brethren: and the first took a wife, and dying left no seed;

units.leftText: Then the second one married the widow, but he also died and left no children. And the third did likewise.
units.rightText: and the second took her, and died, leaving no seed behind him; and the third likewise:

units.leftText: In this way, none of the seven left any children. And last of all, the woman died.
units.rightText: and the seven left no seed. Last of all the woman also died.

units.leftText: In the resurrection, then, whose wife will she be? For all seven were married to her.”
units.rightText: In the resurrection whose wife shall she be of them? for the seven had her to wife.
leftNotes: 12:23 Literally In the resurrection, when they rise,

units.leftText: Jesus said to them, “Aren’t you mistaken, because you do not know the Scriptures or the power of God?
units.rightText: Jesus said unto them, Is it not for this cause that ye err, that ye know not the scriptures, nor the power of God?

units.leftText: When the dead rise, they will neither marry nor be given in marriage. Instead, they will be like the angels in heaven.
units.rightText: For when they shall rise from the dead, they neither marry, nor are given in marriage; but are as angels in heaven.

units.leftText: But concerning the dead rising, have you not read about the burning bush in the Book of Moses, how God told him, ‘I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’ ?
units.rightText: But as touching the dead, that they are raised; have ye not read in the book of Moses, in the place concerning the Bush, how God spake unto him, saying, I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob?
leftNotes: 12:26 Exodus 3:6|EXO 3:6*

units.leftText: He is not the God of the dead, but of the living. You are badly mistaken!” The Greatest Commandment (Deuteronomy 6:1–19|DEU 6:1-19*; Matthew 22:34–40|MAT 22:34-40*)
units.rightText: He is not the God of the dead, but of the living: ye do greatly err.

units.leftText: Now one of the scribes had come up and heard their debate. Noticing how well Jesus had answered them, he asked Him, “Which commandment is the most important of all?”
units.rightText: And one of the scribes came, and heard them questioning together, and knowing that he had answered them well, asked him, What commandment is the first of all?

units.leftText: Jesus replied, “This is the most important: ‘Hear, O Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is One.
units.rightText: Jesus answered, The first is, Hear, O Israel; The Lord our God, the Lord is one:

units.leftText: Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind and with all your strength.’
units.rightText: and thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind, and with all thy strength.
leftNotes: 12:30 Deuteronomy 6:4–5|DEU 6:4-5*

units.leftText: The second is this: ‘Love your neighbor as yourself.’ No other commandment is greater than these.”
units.rightText: The second is this, Thou shalt love thy neighbor as thyself. There is none other commandment greater than these.
leftNotes: 12:31 Leviticus 19:18|LEV 19:18*

units.leftText: “Right, Teacher,” the scribe replied. “You have stated correctly that God is One and there is no other but Him,
units.rightText: And the scribe said unto him, Of a truth, Teacher, thou hast well said that he is one; and there is none other but he:

units.leftText: and to love Him with all your heart and with all your understanding and with all your strength, and to love your neighbor as yourself. This is more important than all burnt offerings and sacrifices.”
units.rightText: and to love him with all the heart, and with all the understanding, and with all the strength, and to love his neighbor as himself, is much more than all whole burnt-offerings and sacrifices.

units.leftText: When Jesus saw that the man had answered wisely, He said, “You are not far from the kingdom of God.” And no one dared to question Him any further. Whose Son Is the Christ? (Matthew 22:41–46|MAT 22:41-46*; Luke 20:41–44|LUK 20:41-44*)
units.rightText: And when Jesus saw that he answered discreetly, he said unto him, Thou art not far from the kingdom of God. And no man after that durst ask him any question.

units.leftText: While Jesus was teaching in the temple courts, He asked, “How can the scribes say that the Christ is the Son of David?
units.rightText: And Jesus answered and said, as he taught in the temple, How say the scribes that the Christ is the son of David?
leftNotes: 12:35 Literally the temple

units.leftText: Speaking by the Holy Spirit, David himself declared: ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at My right hand until I put Your enemies under Your feet.”’
units.rightText: David himself said in the Holy Spirit, The Lord said unto my Lord, Sit thou on my right hand, Till I make thine enemies the footstool of thy feet.

units.leftText: David himself calls Him ‘Lord.’ So how can He be David’s son?” And the large crowd listened to Him with delight. Beware of the Scribes (Luke 20:45–47|LUK 20:45-47*)
units.rightText: David himself calleth him Lord; and whence is he his son? And the common people heard him gladly.

units.leftText: In His teaching Jesus also said, “Watch out for the scribes. They like to walk around in long robes, to receive greetings in the marketplaces,
units.rightText: And in his teaching he said, Beware of the scribes, who desire to walk in long robes, and to have salutations in the marketplaces,

units.leftText: and to have the chief seats in the synagogues and the places of honor at banquets.
units.rightText: and chief seats in the synagogues, and chief places at feasts:

units.leftText: They defraud widows of their houses, and for a show make lengthy prayers. These men will receive greater condemnation.” The Widow’s Offering (Luke 21:1–4|LUK 21:1-4*)
units.rightText: they that devour widows’ houses, and for a pretence make long prayers; these shall receive greater condemnation.
leftNotes: 12:40 Literally They devour widows’ houses

units.leftText: As Jesus was sitting opposite the treasury, He watched the crowd putting money into it. And many rich people put in large amounts.
units.rightText: And he sat down over against the treasury, and beheld how the multitude cast money into the treasury: and many that were rich cast in much.

units.leftText: Then one poor widow came and put in two small copper coins, which amounted to a small fraction of a denarius.
units.rightText: And there came a poor widow, and she cast in two mites, which make a farthing.
leftNotes: 12:42 Greek put in two lepta, which is a kodrantēs; a lepton was a Jewish coin of bronze or copper worth about 1/128 of a denarius.

units.leftText: Jesus called His disciples to Him and said, “Truly I tell you, this poor widow has put more than all the others into the treasury.
units.rightText: And he called unto him his disciples, and said unto them, Verily I say unto you, This poor widow cast in more than all they that are casting into the treasury:

units.leftText: For they all contributed out of their surplus, but she out of her poverty has put in all she had to live on.”
units.rightText: for they all did cast in of their superfluity; but she of her want did cast in all that she had, even all her living.

units.leftText: As Jesus was leaving the temple, one of His disciples said to Him, “Teacher, look at the magnificent stones and buildings!”
units.rightText: And as he went forth out of the temple, one of his disciples saith unto him, Teacher, behold, what manner of stones and what manner of buildings!

units.leftText: “Do you see all these great buildings?” Jesus replied. “Not one stone here will be left on another; every one will be thrown down.”
units.rightText: And Jesus said unto him, Seest thou these great buildings? there shall not be left here one stone upon another, which shall not be thrown down.

units.leftText: While Jesus was sitting on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, Peter, James, John, and Andrew asked Him privately,
units.rightText: And as he sat on the mount of Olives over against the temple, Peter and James and John and Andrew asked him privately,

units.leftText: “Tell us, when will these things happen? And what will be the sign that they are about to be fulfilled?”
units.rightText: Tell us, when shall these things be? and what shall be the sign when these things are all about to be accomplished?

units.leftText: Jesus began by telling them, “See to it that no one deceives you.
units.rightText: And Jesus began to say unto them, Take heed that no man lead you astray.

units.leftText: Many will come in My name, claiming, ‘I am He,’ and will deceive many.
units.rightText: Many shall come in my name, saying, I am he; and shall lead many astray.

units.leftText: When you hear of wars and rumors of wars, do not be alarmed. These things must happen, but the end is still to come.
units.rightText: And when ye shall hear of wars and rumors of wars, be not troubled: these things must needs come to pass; but the end is not yet.

units.leftText: Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. There will be earthquakes in various places, as well as famines. These are the beginning of birth pains. Witnessing to All Nations (Matthew 24:9–14|MAT 24:9-14*; Luke 21:10–19|LUK 21:10-19*)
units.rightText: For nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom; there shall be earthquakes in divers places; there shall be famines: these things are the beginning of travail.

units.leftText: So be on your guard. You will be delivered over to the councils and beaten in the synagogues. On My account you will stand before governors and kings as witnesses to them.
units.rightText: But take ye heed to yourselves: for they shall deliver you up to councils; and in synagogues shall ye be beaten; and before governors and kings shall ye stand for my sake, for a testimony unto them.

units.leftText: And the gospel must first be proclaimed to all the nations.
units.rightText: And the gospel must first be preached unto all the nations.

units.leftText: But when they arrest you and hand you over, do not worry beforehand what to say. Instead, speak whatever you are given at that time, for it will not be you speaking, but the Holy Spirit.
units.rightText: And when they lead you to judgment, and deliver you up, be not anxious beforehand what ye shall speak: but whatsoever shall be given you in that hour, that speak ye; for it is not ye that speak, but the Holy Spirit.

units.leftText: Brother will betray brother to death, and a father his child. Children will rise against their parents and have them put to death.
units.rightText: And brother shall deliver up brother to death, and the father his child; and children shall rise up against parents, and cause them to be put to death.

units.leftText: You will be hated by everyone because of My name, but the one who perseveres to the end will be saved. The Abomination of Desolation (Matthew 24:15–25|MAT 24:15-25*; Luke 21:20–24|LUK 21:20-24*)
units.rightText: And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake: but he that endureth to the end, the same shall be saved.

units.leftText: So when you see the abomination of desolation standing where it should not be (let the reader understand), then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains.
units.rightText: But when ye see the abomination of desolation standing where he ought not (let him that readeth understand), then let them that are in Judæa flee unto the mountains:
leftNotes: 13:14 See Daniel 9:27|DAN 9:27*, Daniel 11:31, and Daniel 12:11; BYZ and TR include spoken of by Daniel the prophet.
13:14 Or where he should not be

units.leftText: Let no one on the housetop go back inside to retrieve anything from his house.
units.rightText: and let him that is on the housetop not go down, nor enter in, to take anything out of his house:

units.leftText: And let no one in the field return for his cloak.
units.rightText: and let him that is in the field not return back to take his cloak.

units.leftText: How miserable those days will be for pregnant and nursing mothers!
units.rightText: But woe unto them that are with child and to them that give suck in those days!

units.leftText: Pray that this will not occur in the winter.
units.rightText: And pray ye that it be not in the winter.

units.leftText: For those will be days of tribulation unseen from the beginning of God’s creation until now, and never to be seen again.
units.rightText: For those days shall be tribulation, such as there hath not been the like from the beginning of the creation which God created until now, and never shall be.

units.leftText: If the Lord had not cut short those days, nobody would be saved. But for the sake of the elect, whom He has chosen, He has cut them short.
units.rightText: And except the Lord had shortened the days, no flesh would have been saved; but for the elect’s sake, whom he chose, he shortened the days.

units.leftText: At that time if anyone says to you, ‘Look, here is the Christ!’ or ‘There He is!’ do not believe it.
units.rightText: And then if any man shall say unto you, Lo, here is the Christ; or, Lo, there; believe it not:

units.leftText: For false Christs and false prophets will appear and perform signs and wonders to deceive even the elect, if that were possible.
units.rightText: for there shall arise false Christs and false prophets, and shall show signs and wonders, that they may lead astray, if possible, the elect.

units.leftText: So be on your guard; I have told you everything in advance. The Return of the Son of Man (Matthew 24:26–31|MAT 24:26-31*; Luke 21:25–28|LUK 21:25-28*)
units.rightText: But take ye heed: behold, I have told you all things beforehand.

units.leftText: But in those days, after that tribulation: ‘The sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light;
units.rightText: But in those days, after that tribulation, the sun shall be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light,

units.leftText: the stars will fall from the sky, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.’
units.rightText: and the stars shall be falling from heaven, and the powers that are in the heavens shall be shaken.
leftNotes: 13:25 Or and the celestial bodies will be shaken; see Isaiah 13:10|ISA 13:10*, Isaiah 34:4, and Joel 2:10.

units.leftText: At that time they will see the Son of Man coming in the clouds with great power and glory.
units.rightText: And then shall they see the Son of man coming in clouds with great power and glory.

units.leftText: And He will send out the angels to gather His elect from the four winds, from the ends of the earth to the ends of heaven. The Lesson of the Fig Tree (Matthew 24:32–35|MAT 24:32-35*; Luke 21:29–33|LUK 21:29-33*)
units.rightText: And then shall he send forth the angels, and shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from the uttermost part of the earth to the uttermost part of heaven.

units.leftText: Now learn this lesson from the fig tree: As soon as its branches become tender and sprout leaves, you know that summer is near.
units.rightText: Now from the fig tree learn her parable: when her branch is now become tender, and putteth forth its leaves, ye know that the summer is nigh;
leftNotes: 13:28 Or this parable

units.leftText: So also, when you see these things happening, know that He is near, right at the door.
units.rightText: even so ye also, when ye see these things coming to pass, know ye that he is nigh, even at the doors.
leftNotes: 13:29 Or it is near

units.leftText: Truly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until all these things have happened.
units.rightText: Verily I say unto you, This generation shall not pass away, until all these things be accomplished.

units.leftText: Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will never pass away. Readiness at Any Hour (Matthew 24:36–51|MAT 24:36-51*; Luke 12:35–48|LUK 12:35-48*)
units.rightText: Heaven and earth shall pass away: but my words shall not pass away.

units.leftText: No one knows about that day or hour, not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but only the Father.
units.rightText: But of that day or that hour knoweth no one, not even the angels in heaven, neither the Son, but the Father.

units.leftText: Be on your guard and stay alert! For you do not know when the appointed time will come.
units.rightText: Take ye heed, watch and pray: for ye know not when the time is.
leftNotes: 13:33 BYZ and TR Be on your guard, stay alert, and pray!

units.leftText: It is like a man going on a journey who left his house, put each servant in charge of his own task, and instructed the doorkeeper to keep watch.
units.rightText: It is as when a man, sojourning in another country, having left his house, and given authority to his servants, to each one his work, commanded also the porter to watch.

units.leftText: Therefore keep watch, because you do not know when the master of the house will return — whether in the evening, at midnight, when the rooster crows, or in the morning.
units.rightText: Watch therefore: for ye know not when the lord of the house cometh, whether at even, or at midnight, or at cockcrowing, or in the morning;

units.leftText: Otherwise, he may arrive without notice and find you sleeping.
units.rightText: lest coming suddenly he find you sleeping.

units.leftText: And what I say to you, I say to everyone: Keep watch!”
units.rightText: And what I say unto you I say unto all, Watch.

units.leftText: Now the Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread were two days away, and the chief priests and scribes were looking for a covert way to arrest Jesus and kill Him.
units.rightText: Now after two days was the feast of the passover and the unleavened bread: and the chief priests and the scribes sought how they might take him with subtlety, and kill him:
leftNotes: 14:1 Literally and the Unleavened; see Exodus 12:14–20|EXO 12:14-20*.

units.leftText: “But not during the feast,” they said, “or there may be a riot among the people.” Jesus Anointed at Bethany (Matthew 26:6–13|MAT 26:6-13*; Luke 7:36–50|LUK 7:36-50*; John 12:1–8|JHN 12:1-8*)
units.rightText: for they said, Not during the feast, lest haply there shall be a tumult of the people.

units.leftText: While Jesus was in Bethany reclining at the table in the home of Simon the Leper, a woman came with an alabaster jar of expensive perfume, made of pure nard. She broke open the jar and poured it on Jesus’ head.
units.rightText: And while he was in Bethany in the house of Simon the leper, as he sat at meat, there came a woman having an alabaster cruse of ointment of pure nard very costly; and she brake the cruse, and poured it over his head.
leftNotes: 14:3 Aramaic Simon the Potter or Simon the Jar Maker

units.leftText: Some of those present, however, expressed their indignation to one another: “Why this waste of perfume?
units.rightText: But there were some that had indignation among themselves, saying, To what purpose hath this waste of the ointment been made?

units.leftText: It could have been sold for over three hundred denarii and the money given to the poor.” And they scolded her.
units.rightText: For this ointment might have been sold for above three hundred shillings, and given to the poor. And they murmured against her.
leftNotes: 14:5 A denarius was customarily a day’s wage for a laborer; see Matthew 20:2|MAT 20:2*.

units.leftText: But Jesus said, “Leave her alone; why are you bothering her? She has done a beautiful deed to Me.
units.rightText: But Jesus said, Let her alone; why trouble ye her? she hath wrought a good work on me.

units.leftText: The poor you will always have with you, and you can help them whenever you want. But you will not always have Me.
units.rightText: For ye have the poor always with you, and whensoever ye will ye can do them good: but me ye have not always.
leftNotes: 14:7 See Deuteronomy 15:11|DEU 15:11*.

units.leftText: She has done what she could to anoint My body in advance of My burial.
units.rightText: She hath done what she could; she hath anointed my body beforehand for the burying.

units.leftText: And truly I tell you, wherever the gospel is preached in all the world, what she has done will also be told in memory of her.” Judas Agrees to Betray Jesus (Matthew 26:14–16|MAT 26:14-16*; Luke 22:3–6|LUK 22:3-6*)
units.rightText: And verily I say unto you, Wheresoever the gospel shall be preached throughout the whole world, that also which this woman hath done shall be spoken of for a memorial of her.

units.leftText: Then Judas Iscariot, one of the Twelve, went to the chief priests to betray Jesus to them.
units.rightText: And Judas Iscariot, he that was one of the twelve, went away unto the chief priests, that he might deliver him unto them.

units.leftText: They were delighted to hear this, and they promised to give him money. So Judas began to look for an opportunity to betray Jesus. Preparing the Passover (Matthew 26:17–19|MAT 26:17-19*; Luke 22:7–13|LUK 22:7-13*)
units.rightText: And they, when they heard it, were glad, and promised to give him money. And he sought how he might conveniently deliver him unto them.

units.leftText: On the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, when the Passover lamb was to be sacrificed, Jesus’ disciples asked Him, “Where do You want us to prepare for You to eat the Passover?”
units.rightText: And on the first day of unleavened bread, when they sacrificed the passover, his disciples say unto him, Where wilt thou that we go and make ready that thou mayest eat the passover?
leftNotes: 14:12 Literally On the first day of the Unleavened; see Exodus 12:14–20|EXO 12:14-20*.

units.leftText: So He sent two of His disciples and told them, “Go into the city, and a man carrying a jug of water will meet you. Follow him,
units.rightText: And he sendeth two of his disciples, and saith unto them, Go into the city, and there shall meet you a man bearing a pitcher of water: follow him;

units.leftText: and whichever house he enters, say to the owner, ‘The Teacher asks: Where is My guest room, where I may eat the Passover with My disciples?’
units.rightText: and wheresoever he shall enter in, say to the master of the house, The Teacher saith, Where is my guest-chamber, where I shall eat the passover with my disciples?

units.leftText: And he will show you a large upper room, furnished and ready. Make preparations for us there.”
units.rightText: And he will himself show you a large upper room furnished and ready: and there make ready for us.

units.leftText: So the disciples left and went into the city, where they found everything as Jesus had described. And they prepared the Passover. The Last Supper (Matthew 26:20–30|MAT 26:20-30*; Luke 22:14–23|LUK 22:14-23*; 1 Corinthians 11:17–34|1CO 11:17-34*)
units.rightText: And the disciples went forth, and came into the city, and found as he had said unto them: and they made ready the passover.

units.leftText: When evening came, Jesus arrived with the Twelve.
units.rightText: And when it was evening he cometh with the twelve.

units.leftText: And while they were reclining and eating, Jesus said, “Truly I tell you, one of you who is eating with Me will betray Me.”
units.rightText: And as they sat and were eating, Jesus said, Verily I say unto you, One of you shall betray me, even he that eateth with me.

units.leftText: They began to be grieved and to ask Him one after another, “Surely not I?”
units.rightText: They began to be sorrowful, and to say unto him one by one, Is it I?

units.leftText: He answered, “It is one of the Twelve — the one who is dipping his hand into the bowl with Me.
units.rightText: And he said unto them, It is one of the twelve, he that dippeth with me in the dish.
leftNotes: 14:20 Literally the one who is dipping

units.leftText: The Son of Man will go just as it is written about Him, but woe to that man by whom He is betrayed! It would be better for him if he had not been born.”
units.rightText: For the Son of man goeth, even as it is written of him: but woe unto that man through whom the Son of man is betrayed! good were it for that man if he had not been born.

units.leftText: While they were eating, Jesus took bread, spoke a blessing and broke it, and gave it to the disciples, saying, “Take it; this is My body.”
units.rightText: And as they were eating, he took bread, and when he had blessed, he brake it, and gave to them, and said, Take ye: this is my body.

units.leftText: Then He took the cup, gave thanks, and gave it to them, and they all drank from it.
units.rightText: And he took a cup, and when he had given thanks, he gave to them: and they all drank of it.

units.leftText: He said to them, “This is My blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many.
units.rightText: And he said unto them, This is my blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many.
leftNotes: 14:24 BYZ and TR the new covenant

units.leftText: Truly I tell you, I will no longer drink of the fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it anew in the kingdom of God.”
units.rightText: Verily I say unto you, I shall no more drink of the fruit of the vine, until that day when I drink it new in the kingdom of God.

units.leftText: And when they had sung a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives. Jesus Predicts Peter’s Denial (Zechariah 13:7–9|ZEC 13:7-9*; Matthew 26:31–35|MAT 26:31-35*; Luke 22:31–38|LUK 22:31-38*; John 13:36–38|JHN 13:36-38*)
units.rightText: And when they had sung a hymn, they went out unto the mount of Olives.

units.leftText: Then Jesus said to them, “You will all fall away, for it is written: ‘I will strike the Shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.’
units.rightText: And Jesus saith unto them, All ye shall be offended: for it is written, I will smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered abroad.
leftNotes: 14:27 BYZ and TR include on account of Me this night; see Matthew 26:31|MAT 26:31*.
14:27 Zechariah 13:7|ZEC 13:7*

units.leftText: But after I have risen, I will go ahead of you into Galilee.”
units.rightText: Howbeit, after I am raised up, I will go before you into Galilee.

units.leftText: Peter declared, “Even if all fall away, I never will.”
units.rightText: But Peter said unto him, Although all shall be offended, yet will not I.

units.leftText: “Truly I tell you,” Jesus replied, “this very night, before the rooster crows twice, you will deny Me three times.”
units.rightText: And Jesus saith unto him, Verily I say unto thee, that thou to-day, even this night, before the cock crow twice, shalt deny me thrice.

units.leftText: But Peter kept insisting, “Even if I have to die with You, I will never deny You.” And all the others said the same thing. Jesus Prays at Gethsemane (Matthew 26:36–46|MAT 26:36-46*; Luke 22:39–46|LUK 22:39-46*)
units.rightText: But he spake exceeding vehemently, If I must die with thee, I will not deny thee. And in like manner also said they all.

units.leftText: Then they came to a place called Gethsemane, and Jesus told His disciples, “Sit here while I pray.”
units.rightText: And they come unto a place which was named Gethsemane: and he saith unto his disciples, Sit ye here, while I pray.

units.leftText: He took with Him Peter, James, and John, and began to be deeply troubled and distressed.
units.rightText: And he taketh with him Peter and James and John, and began to be greatly amazed, and sore troubled.
