units.leftText: Then He said to them, “My soul is consumed with sorrow to the point of death. Stay here and keep watch.”
units.rightText: And he saith unto them, My soul is exceeding sorrowful even unto death: abide ye here, and watch.

units.leftText: Going a little farther, He fell to the ground and prayed that, if it were possible, the hour would pass from Him.
units.rightText: And he went forward a little, and fell on the ground, and prayed that, if it were possible, the hour might pass away from him.

units.leftText: “Abba, Father,” He said, “all things are possible for You. Take this cup from Me. Yet not what I will, but what You will.”
units.rightText: And he said, Abba, Father, all things are possible unto thee; remove this cup from me: howbeit not what I will, but what thou wilt.

units.leftText: Then Jesus returned and found them sleeping. “Simon, are you asleep?” He asked. “Were you not able to keep watch for one hour?
units.rightText: And he cometh, and findeth them sleeping, and saith unto Peter, Simon, sleepest thou? couldest thou not watch one hour?

units.leftText: Watch and pray so that you will not enter into temptation. For the spirit is willing, but the body is weak.”
units.rightText: Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptation: the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.

units.leftText: Again He went away and prayed, saying the same thing.
units.rightText: And again he went away, and prayed, saying the same words.

units.leftText: And again Jesus returned and found them sleeping, for their eyes were heavy. And they did not know what to answer Him.
units.rightText: And again he came, and found them sleeping, for their eyes were very heavy; and they knew not what to answer him.

units.leftText: When Jesus returned the third time, He said, “Are you still sleeping and resting? That is enough! The hour has come. Look, the Son of Man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.
units.rightText: And he cometh the third time, and saith unto them, Sleep on now, and take your rest: it is enough; the hour is come; behold, the Son of man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.

units.leftText: Rise, let us go. See, My betrayer is approaching!” The Betrayal of Jesus (Matthew 26:47–56|MAT 26:47-56*; Luke 22:47–53|LUK 22:47-53*; John 18:1–14|JHN 18:1-14*)
units.rightText: Arise, let us be going: behold, he that betrayeth me is at hand.

units.leftText: While Jesus was still speaking, Judas, one of the Twelve, arrived, accompanied by a crowd armed with swords and clubs, sent from the chief priests, scribes, and elders.
units.rightText: And straightway, while he yet spake, cometh Judas, one of the twelve, and with him a multitude with swords and staves, from the chief priests and the scribes and the elders.

units.leftText: Now the betrayer had arranged a signal with them: “The One I kiss is the man; arrest Him and lead Him away securely.”
units.rightText: Now he that betrayed him had given them a token, saying, Whomsoever I shall kiss, that is he; take him, and lead him away safely.

units.leftText: Going directly to Jesus, he said, “Rabbi!” and kissed Him.
units.rightText: And when he was come, straightway he came to him, and saith, Rabbi; and kissed him.

units.leftText: Then the men seized Jesus and arrested Him.
units.rightText: And they laid hands on him, and took him.

units.leftText: And one of the bystanders drew his sword and struck the servant of the high priest, cutting off his ear.
units.rightText: But a certain one of them that stood by drew his sword, and smote the servant of the high priest, and struck off his ear.

units.leftText: Jesus asked the crowd, “Have you come out with swords and clubs to arrest Me as you would an outlaw?
units.rightText: And Jesus answered and said unto them, Are ye come out, as against a robber, with swords and staves to seize me?

units.leftText: Every day I was with you, teaching in the temple courts, and you did not arrest Me. But this has happened that the Scriptures would be fulfilled.”
units.rightText: I was daily with you in the temple teaching, and ye took me not: but this is done that the scriptures might be fulfilled.
leftNotes: 14:49 Literally the temple

units.leftText: Then everyone deserted Him and fled.
units.rightText: And they all left him, and fled.

units.leftText: One young man who had been following Jesus was wearing a linen cloth around his body. They caught hold of him,
units.rightText: And a certain young man followed with him, having a linen cloth cast about him, over his naked body: and they lay hold on him;

units.leftText: but he pulled free of the linen cloth and ran away naked. Jesus before the Sanhedrin (Matthew 26:57–68|MAT 26:57-68*; Luke 22:66–71|LUK 22:66-71*; John 18:19–24|JHN 18:19-24*)
units.rightText: but he left the linen cloth, and fled naked.

units.leftText: They led Jesus away to the high priest, and all the chief priests, elders, and scribes assembled.
units.rightText: And they led Jesus away to the high priest: and there come together with him all the chief priests and the elders and the scribes.

units.leftText: Peter followed Him at a distance, right into the courtyard of the high priest. And he sat with the officers and warmed himself by the fire.
units.rightText: And Peter had followed him afar off, even within, into the court of the high priest; and he was sitting with the officers, and warming himself in the light of the fire.

units.leftText: Now the chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin were seeking testimony against Jesus to put Him to death, but they did not find any.
units.rightText: Now the chief priests and the whole council sought witness against Jesus to put him to death; and found it not.
leftNotes: 14:55 Or the whole Council

units.leftText: For many bore false witness against Jesus, but their testimony was inconsistent.
units.rightText: For many bare false witness against him, and their witness agreed not together.

units.leftText: Then some men stood up and testified falsely against Him:
units.rightText: And there stood up certain, and bare false witness against him, saying,

units.leftText: “We heard Him say, ‘I will destroy this man-made temple, and in three days I will build another that is made without hands.’”
units.rightText: We heard him say, I will destroy this temple that is made with hands, and in three days I will build another made without hands.

units.leftText: But even their testimony was inconsistent.
units.rightText: And not even so did their witness agree together.

units.leftText: So the high priest stood up before them and questioned Jesus, “Have You no answer? What are these men testifying against You?”
units.rightText: And the high priest stood up in the midst, and asked Jesus, saying, Answerest thou nothing? what is it which these witness against thee?

units.leftText: But Jesus remained silent and made no reply. Again the high priest questioned Him, “Are You the Christ, the Son of the Blessed One?”
units.rightText: But he held his peace, and answered nothing. Again the high priest asked him, and saith unto him, Art thou the Christ, the Son of the Blessed?

units.leftText: “I am,” said Jesus, “and you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power and coming with the clouds of heaven.”
units.rightText: And Jesus said, I am: and ye shall see the Son of man sitting at the right hand of Power, and coming with the clouds of heaven.
leftNotes: 14:62 Or the right hand of the Mighty One
14:62 See Psalm 110:1|PSA 110:1* and Daniel 7:13.

units.leftText: At this, the high priest tore his clothes and declared, “Why do we need any more witnesses?
units.rightText: And the high priest rent his clothes, and saith, What further need have we of witnesses?

units.leftText: You have heard the blasphemy. What is your verdict?” And they all condemned Him as deserving of death.
units.rightText: Ye have heard the blasphemy: what think ye? And they all condemned him to be worthy of death.

units.leftText: Then some of them began to spit on Him. They blindfolded Him, struck Him with their fists, and said to Him, “Prophesy!” And the officers received Him with slaps in His face. Peter Denies Jesus (Matthew 26:69–75|MAT 26:69-75*; Luke 22:54–62|LUK 22:54-62*; John 18:15–18|JHN 18:15-18*)
units.rightText: And some began to spit on him, and to cover his face, and to buffet him, and to say unto him, Prophesy: and the officers received him with blows of their hands.

units.leftText: While Peter was in the courtyard below, one of the servant girls of the high priest came down
units.rightText: And as Peter was beneath in the court, there cometh one of the maids of the high priest;

units.leftText: and saw him warming himself there. She looked at Peter and said, “You also were with Jesus the Nazarene.”
units.rightText: and seeing Peter warming himself, she looked upon him, and saith, Thou also wast with the Nazarene, even Jesus.

units.leftText: But he denied it. “I do not know or even understand what you are talking about,” he said. Then he went out to the gateway, and the rooster crowed.
units.rightText: But he denied, saying, I neither know, nor understand what thou sayest: and he went out into the porch; and the cock crew.
leftNotes: 14:68 NE and WH do not include and the rooster crowed.

units.leftText: There the servant girl saw him and again said to those standing nearby, “This man is one of them.”
units.rightText: And the maid saw him, and began again to say to them that stood by, This is one of them.

units.leftText: But he denied it again. After a little while, those standing nearby said once more to Peter, “Surely you are one of them, for you too are a Galilean.”
units.rightText: But he again denied it. And after a little while again they that stood by said to Peter, Of a truth thou art one of them; for thou art a Galilæan.
leftNotes: 14:70 BYZ and TR include and your speech is similar.

units.leftText: But he began to curse and swear, “I do not know this man of whom you speak!”
units.rightText: But he began to curse, and to swear, I know not this man of whom ye speak.

units.leftText: And immediately the rooster crowed a second time. Then Peter remembered the word that Jesus had spoken to him: “Before the rooster crows twice, you will deny Me three times.” And he broke down and wept.
units.rightText: And straightway the second time the cock crew. And Peter called to mind the word, how that Jesus said unto him, Before the cock crow twice, thou shalt deny me thrice. And when he thought thereon, he wept.

units.leftText: Early in the morning, the chief priests, elders, scribes, and the whole Sanhedrin devised a plan. They bound Jesus, led Him away, and handed Him over to Pilate.
units.rightText: And straightway in the morning the chief priests with the elders and scribes, and the whole council, held a consultation, and bound Jesus, and carried him away, and delivered him up to Pilate.
leftNotes: 15:1 Or the whole Council

units.leftText: So Pilate questioned Him, “Are You the King of the Jews?” “You have said so,” Jesus replied.
units.rightText: And Pilate asked him, Art thou the King of the Jews? And he answering saith unto him, Thou sayest.

units.leftText: And the chief priests began to accuse Him of many things.
units.rightText: And the chief priests accused him of many things.

units.leftText: Then Pilate questioned Him again, “Have You no answer? Look how many charges they are bringing against You!”
units.rightText: And Pilate again asked him, saying, Answerest thou nothing? behold how many things they accuse thee of.

units.leftText: But to Pilate’s amazement, Jesus made no further reply. The Crowd Chooses Barabbas (Matthew 27:15–23|MAT 27:15-23*; Luke 23:13–25|LUK 23:13-25*)
units.rightText: But Jesus no more answered anything; insomuch that Pilate marvelled.

units.leftText: Now it was Pilate’s custom at the feast to release to the people a prisoner of their choosing.
units.rightText: Now at the feast he used to release unto them one prisoner, whom they asked of him.
leftNotes: 15:6 Literally Now at the feast he would release to them

units.leftText: And a man named Barabbas was imprisoned with the rebels who had committed murder during the insurrection.
units.rightText: And there was one called Barabbas, lying bound with them that had made insurrection, men who in the insurrection had committed murder.

units.leftText: So the crowd went up and began asking Pilate to keep his custom.
units.rightText: And the multitude went up and began to ask him to do as he was wont to do unto them.

units.leftText: “Do you want me to release to you the King of the Jews?” Pilate asked.
units.rightText: And Pilate answered them, saying, Will ye that I release unto you the King of the Jews?

units.leftText: For he knew it was out of envy that the chief priests had handed Jesus over.
units.rightText: For he perceived that for envy the chief priests had delivered him up.

units.leftText: But the chief priests stirred up the crowd to have him release Barabbas to them instead. Pilate Delivers Up Jesus (Matthew 27:24–26|MAT 27:24-26*)
units.rightText: But the chief priests stirred up the multitude, that he should rather release Barabbas unto them.

units.leftText: So Pilate asked them again, “What then do you want me to do with the One you call the King of the Jews?”
units.rightText: And Pilate again answered and said unto them, What then shall I do unto him whom ye call the King of the Jews?

units.leftText: And they shouted back, “Crucify Him!”
units.rightText: And they cried out again, Crucify him.

units.leftText: “Why?” asked Pilate. “What evil has He done?” But they shouted all the louder, “Crucify Him!”
units.rightText: And Pilate said unto them, Why, what evil hath he done? But they cried out exceedingly, Crucify him.

units.leftText: And wishing to satisfy the crowd, Pilate released Barabbas to them. But he had Jesus flogged, and handed Him over to be crucified. The Soldiers Mock Jesus (Isaiah 50:4–11|ISA 50:4-11*; Matthew 27:27–31|MAT 27:27-31*; Luke 22:63–65|LUK 22:63-65*; John 19:1–15|JHN 19:1-15*)
units.rightText: And Pilate, wishing to content the multitude, released unto them Barabbas, and delivered Jesus, when he had scourged him, to be crucified.

units.leftText: Then the soldiers led Jesus away into the palace (that is, the Praetorium) and called the whole company together.
units.rightText: And the soldiers led him away within the court, which is the Prætorium; and they call together the whole band.

units.leftText: They dressed Him in a purple robe, twisted together a crown of thorns, and set it on His head.
units.rightText: And they clothe him with purple, and platting a crown of thorns, they put it on him;

units.leftText: And they began to salute Him: “Hail, King of the Jews!”
units.rightText: and they began to salute him, Hail, King of the Jews!

units.leftText: They kept striking His head with a staff and spitting on Him. And they knelt down and bowed before Him.
units.rightText: And they smote his head with a reed, and spat upon him, and bowing their knees worshipped him.

units.leftText: After they had mocked Him, they removed the purple robe and put His own clothes back on Him. Then they led Him out to crucify Him. The Crucifixion (Psalm 22:1–31|PSA 22:1-31*; Matthew 27:32–44|MAT 27:32-44*; Luke 23:26–43|LUK 23:26-43*; John 19:16–27|JHN 19:16-27*)
units.rightText: And when they had mocked him, they took off from him the purple, and put on him his garments. And they lead him out to crucify him.

units.leftText: Now Simon of Cyrene, the father of Alexander and Rufus, was passing by on his way in from the country, and the soldiers forced him to carry the cross of Jesus.
units.rightText: And they compel one passing by, Simon of Cyrene, coming from the country, the father of Alexander and Rufus, to go with them, that he might bear his cross.

units.leftText: They brought Jesus to a place called Golgotha, which means The Place of the Skull.
units.rightText: And they bring him unto the place Golgotha, which is, being interpreted, The place of a skull.

units.leftText: There they offered Him wine mixed with myrrh, but He did not take it.
units.rightText: And they offered him wine mingled with myrrh: but he received it not.

units.leftText: And they crucified Him. They also divided His garments by casting lots to decide what each of them would take.
units.rightText: And they crucify him, and part his garments among them, casting lots upon them, what each should take.

units.leftText: It was the third hour when they crucified Him.
units.rightText: And it was the third hour, and they crucified him.
leftNotes: 15:25 That is, nine in the morning

units.leftText: And the charge inscribed against Him read: THE KING OF THE JEWS.
units.rightText: And the superscription of his accusation was written over, THE KING OF THE JEWS.

units.leftText: Along with Jesus, they crucified two robbers, one on His right and one on His left.
units.rightText: And with him they crucify two robbers; one on his right hand, and one on his left.
leftNotes: 15:27 Or insurrectionists
15:27 BYZ and TR include 28*So the Scripture was fulfilled that says, “And He was numbered with the transgressors.”See Isaiah 53:12|ISA 53:12* and Luke 22:37.

rightNotes: 15:28 Many ancient authorities insert v. 28, And the scripture was fulfilled, which saith, And he was reckoned with transgressors. See luk 22:37.

units.leftText: And those who passed by heaped abuse on Him, shaking their heads and saying, “Aha! You who are going to destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days,
units.rightText: And they that passed by railed on him, wagging their heads, and saying, Ha! thou that destroyest the temple, and buildest it in three days,

units.leftText: come down from the cross and save Yourself!”
units.rightText: save thyself, and come down from the cross.

units.leftText: In the same way, the chief priests and scribes mocked Him among themselves, saying, “He saved others, but He cannot save Himself!
units.rightText: In like manner also the chief priests mocking him among themselves with the scribes said, He saved others; himself he cannot save.

units.leftText: Let the Christ, the King of Israel, come down now from the cross, so that we may see and believe!” And even those who were crucified with Him berated Him. The Death of Jesus (Psalm 22:1–31|PSA 22:1-31*; Matthew 27:45–56|MAT 27:45-56*; Luke 23:44–49|LUK 23:44-49*; John 19:28–30|JHN 19:28-30*)
units.rightText: Let the Christ, the King of Israel, now come down from the cross, that we may see and believe. And they that were crucified with him reproached him.

units.leftText: From the sixth hour until the ninth hour darkness came over all the land.
units.rightText: And when the sixth hour was come, there was darkness over the whole land until the ninth hour.
leftNotes: 15:33 That is, from noon until three in the afternoon

units.leftText: At the ninth hour, Jesus cried out in a loud voice, “Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?” which means, “My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?”
units.rightText: And at the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani? which is, being interpreted, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?

units.leftText: When some of those standing nearby heard this, they said, “Behold, He is calling Elijah.”
units.rightText: And some of them that stood by, when they heard it, said, Behold, he calleth Elijah.

units.leftText: And someone ran and filled a sponge with sour wine. He put it on a reed and held it up for Jesus to drink, saying, “Leave Him alone. Let us see if Elijah comes to take Him down.”
units.rightText: And one ran, and filling a sponge full of vinegar, put it on a reed, and gave him to drink, saying, Let be; let us see whether Elijah cometh to take him down.
leftNotes: 15:36 Or a sponge with wine vinegar

units.leftText: But Jesus let out a loud cry and breathed His last.
units.rightText: And Jesus uttered a loud voice, and gave up the ghost.

units.leftText: And the veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom.
units.rightText: And the veil of the temple was rent in two from the top to the bottom.

units.leftText: When the centurion standing there in front of Jesus saw how He had breathed His last, he said, “Truly this man was the Son of God!”
units.rightText: And when the centurion, who stood by over against him, saw that he so gave up the ghost, he said, Truly this man was the Son of God.
leftNotes: 15:39 BYZ and TR saw how, having cried out, He had breathed His last

units.leftText: And there were also women watching from a distance. Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James the younger and of Joses, and Salome.
units.rightText: And there were also women beholding from afar: among whom were both Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James the less and of Joses, and Salome;
leftNotes: 15:40 Joses is a variant of Joseph; see Matthew 27:56|MAT 27:56*.

units.leftText: These women had followed Jesus and ministered to Him while He was in Galilee, and there were many other women who had come up to Jerusalem with Him. The Burial of Jesus (Isaiah 53:9–12|ISA 53:9-12*; Matthew 27:57–61|MAT 27:57-61*; Luke 23:50–56|LUK 23:50-56*; John 19:38–42|JHN 19:38-42*)
units.rightText: who, when he was in Galilee, followed him, and ministered unto him; and many other women that came up with him unto Jerusalem.

units.leftText: Now it was already evening. Since it was Preparation Day (that is, the day before the Sabbath ),
units.rightText: And when even was now come, because it was the Preparation, that is, the day before the sabbath,

units.leftText: Joseph of Arimathea, a prominent Council member who himself was waiting for the kingdom of God, boldly went to Pilate to ask for the body of Jesus.
units.rightText: there came Joseph of Arimathæa, a councillor of honorable estate, who also himself was looking for the kingdom of God; and he boldly went in unto Pilate, and asked for the body of Jesus.

units.leftText: Pilate was surprised to hear that Jesus was already dead, so he summoned the centurion to ask if this was so.
units.rightText: And Pilate marvelled if he were already dead: and calling unto him the centurion, he asked him whether he had been any while dead.

units.leftText: When Pilate had confirmed it with the centurion, he granted the body to Joseph.
units.rightText: And when he learned it of the centurion, he granted the corpse to Joseph.

units.leftText: So Joseph bought a linen cloth, took down the body of Jesus, wrapped it in the cloth, and placed it in a tomb that had been cut out of the rock. Then he rolled a stone against the entrance to the tomb.
units.rightText: And he bought a linen cloth, and taking him down, wound him in the linen cloth, and laid him in a tomb which had been hewn out of a rock; and he rolled a stone against the door of the tomb.

units.leftText: Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joseph saw where His body was placed.
units.rightText: And Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses beheld where he was laid.
leftNotes: 15:47 Or Joses

units.leftText: When the Sabbath was over, Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome bought spices so they could go and anoint the body of Jesus.
units.rightText: And when the sabbath was past, Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James, and Salome, bought spices, that they might come and anoint him.

units.leftText: Very early on the first day of the week, just after sunrise, they went to the tomb.
units.rightText: And very early on the first day of the week, they come to the tomb when the sun was risen.
leftNotes: 16:2 Literally And very early on the first of the Sabbaths,

units.leftText: They were asking one another, “Who will roll away the stone from the entrance of the tomb?”
units.rightText: And they were saying among themselves, Who shall roll us away the stone from the door of the tomb?

units.leftText: But when they looked up, they saw that the stone had been rolled away, even though it was extremely large.
units.rightText: and looking up, they see that the stone is rolled back: for it was exceeding great.

units.leftText: When they entered the tomb, they saw a young man dressed in a white robe sitting on the right side, and they were alarmed.
units.rightText: And entering into the tomb, they saw a young man sitting on the right side, arrayed in a white robe; and they were amazed.

units.leftText: But he said to them, “Do not be alarmed. You are looking for Jesus the Nazarene, who was crucified. He has risen! He is not here! See the place where they put Him.
units.rightText: And he saith unto them, Be not amazed: ye seek Jesus, the Nazarene, who hath been crucified: he is risen; he is not here: behold, the place where they laid him!

units.leftText: But go, tell His disciples and Peter, ‘He is going ahead of you into Galilee. There you will see Him, just as He told you.’”
units.rightText: But go, tell his disciples and Peter, He goeth before you into Galilee: there shall ye see him, as he said unto you.

units.leftText: So the women left the tomb and ran away, trembling and bewildered. And in their fear they did not say a word to anyone. Jesus Appears to Mary Magdalene (John 20:10–18|JHN 20:10-18*)
units.rightText: And they went out, and fled from the tomb; for trembling and astonishment had come upon them: and they said nothing to any one; for they were afraid.
leftNotes: 16:8 Some early manuscripts end the Gospel of Mark after verse 8. Other manuscripts contain only a short ending, a version of the following: 9*But they quickly reported all these instructions to Peter’s companions. Afterward, Jesus Himself, through them, sent out from east to west the sacred and imperishable proclamation of eternal salvation. Amen.

units.leftText: Early on the first day of the week, after Jesus had risen, He appeared first to Mary Magdalene, from whom He had driven out seven demons.
units.rightText: Now when he was risen early on the first day of the week, he appeared first to Mary Magdalene, from whom he had cast out seven demons.
leftNotes: 16:9 Or After Jesus had risen early on the first day of the week

units.leftText: She went and told those who had been with Him, who were mourning and weeping.
units.rightText: She went and told them that had been with him, as they mourned and wept.

units.leftText: And when they heard that Jesus was alive and she had seen Him, they did not believe it. Jesus Appears to Two Disciples (Luke 24:13–35|LUK 24:13-35*)
units.rightText: And they, when they heard that he was alive, and had been seen of her, disbelieved.

units.leftText: After this, Jesus appeared in a different form to two of them as they walked along in the country.
units.rightText: And after these things he was manifested in another form unto two of them, as they walked, on their way into the country.

units.leftText: And they went back and reported it to the rest, but they did not believe them either. The Great Commission (Matthew 28:16–20|MAT 28:16-20*)
units.rightText: And they went away and told it unto the rest: neither believed they them.

units.leftText: Later, as they were eating, Jesus appeared to the Eleven and rebuked them for their unbelief and hardness of heart, because they did not believe those who had seen Him after He had risen.
units.rightText: And afterward he was manifested unto the eleven themselves as they sat at meat; and he upbraided them with their unbelief and hardness of heart, because they believed not them that had seen him after he was risen.

units.leftText: And He said to them, “Go into all the world and preach the gospel to every creature.
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Go ye into all the world, and preach the gospel to the whole creation.

units.leftText: Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved, but whoever does not believe will be condemned.
units.rightText: He that believeth and is baptized shall be saved; but he that disbelieveth shall be condemned.

units.leftText: And these signs will accompany those who believe: In My name they will drive out demons; they will speak in new tongues;
units.rightText: And these signs shall accompany them that believe: in my name shall they cast out demons; they shall speak with new tongues;
leftNotes: 16:17 WH in tongues

units.leftText: they will pick up snakes with their hands, and if they drink any deadly poison, it will not harm them; they will lay their hands on the sick, and they will be made well.” The Ascension (Luke 24:50–53|LUK 24:50-53*; Acts 1:6–11|ACT 1:6-11*)
units.rightText: they shall take up serpents, and if they drink any deadly thing, it shall in no wise hurt them; they shall lay hands on the sick, and they shall recover.

units.leftText: After the Lord Jesus had spoken to them, He was taken up into heaven and sat down at the right hand of God.
units.rightText: So then the Lord Jesus, after he had spoken unto them, was received up into heaven, and sat down at the right hand of God.
leftNotes: 16:19 ECM, BYZ, and TR After the LORD

units.leftText: And they went out and preached everywhere, and the Lord worked through them, confirming His word by the signs that accompanied it.
units.rightText: And they went forth, and preached everywhere, the Lord working with them, and confirming the word by the signs that followed. Amen.
